i.html: Challice D’Arle
Challice is Crokus Younghand’s crush. While she was in her room half naked, Crokus saw her while stealing her estate’s jewelry
Crokus came back to return the jewelry, introduced himself, and said one day he’ll be in her line of suitors to deliver a formal introduction.
Meanwhile, Sorry stalked Crokus to eliminate Oponn’s Coin-holder and killed a D’Arle estate guard
The D’Arle Estate suspects Crokus for the murder and wants to find and execute him
At Lady Simtal’s Fete, Challice sits at a fountain and cries for Gorlas when she sees Crokus. Crokus kidnaps her into the gardens.
She doesn’t know or care about Crokus, her father hired a Seer that said the Rope’s servant killed the guard
Crokus tries to court her again, but she laughs at him because she has Gorlas who comes from a powerful family. She keeps Crokus a secret because he’s interesting as a thief but nothing more
Councilman Lim

Lim was killed by Rallick Nom. Rallick intended to kill Lady Simtal for ruining Coll’s life after divorcing him, but Oponn’s influence made him pivot and decide it’s better scandal for a dead councilman in her bedchambers
Turban Orr

Turban Orr wants to be neutral with the Malazan Empire, influence a peaceful occupation, and become a Malazan High Fist. He visits Baruk hoping he can sway the sorcerers in favor of neutrality. The neutrality vote was ruined after Lim’s assassination. He sleeps and schemes with Lady Simtal, while Murillio sleeps with Orr’s wife and finesses two invitations to Lady Simtal’s party from her. Turban Orr also contracted the Assassin’s Guild to kill Coll.
At Lady Simtal’s Fete, Orr suspects Circle Breaker as a spy and nearly attacks him, but Rallick steps in and challenges him to a duel. Rallick kills him in the duel.
Murillio had accepted his invitation to spend new years’ evening with Lady Sepharla
Sepharla is now drunkenly asleep on a marble bench in her garden
Delish, Sepharla’s daughter who looks like she can be at least 20 but doesn’t want to think to hard about it, leaves behind her drunken suitor Prelick passed out in the foyer
Delish flirts with Murillio and they have sex in the garden while her mother snores in the background
Just as they finish, Prelick stabs Murillio in the chest claiming ‘The rapist dies!’
Murillio bleeds from his chest and coughs blood, stumbles out of the garden and into the streets and as the house staff try to pull him back

(Gardens of the Moon) Murillio is a Phoenix Inn regular, a duelist, and a flirt. Always seen courting noblewomen. Conspires with Rallick to get revenge on Lady Simtal for destroying Coll’s life. Murillio courts with Councilman Turban Orr’s wife to finesse two invitations to Lady Simtal’s Gedderone’s Eve Fete. Rallick plans to duel Turban Orr, eliminating her strongest ally and obstacle to restoring Coll to the council.

In the middle of their schemes, Kruppe leads the Phoenix Inn regulars out to the Gadrobi Hills on a mission given to him by High Alchemist Baruk. Adjunct Lorn attacks, Murillio was able to pierce her shoulder but she knocks him unconscious with the flat of her blade. He returns with Kruppe to Darujhistan to prioritize Crokus’ safety, accuses Kruppe of being the Eel and has his memory wiped.

At the Fete, Murillio distracts Lady Simtal with sex. Afterwards, Rallick walks into the room to tell her that he killed Turban Orr in a duel and her Assassin’s Guild contract on Coll failed. Murillio tosses a dagger onto the bed for her to kill herself. Murillio feels remorse and prays to Mowri, saying he is lost.

(Memories of Ice) Murillio and Coll are apart of Darujhistan’s emissaries to the war council against the Pannion Domin. They primarily spend their time caring for the Mhybe’s deteriorating health. They plot to help the Mhybe escape and take her into Capustan to find a temple where she can end her suffering and rest. After searching through seven empty temples, Korbal Broach attacks to take the Mhybe, but the Knight of High House Death expels Korbal and Bauchelain from the city. The Temple of Hood prepared a resting place for the Mhybe. While waiting in the temple, Murillio admits to Coll that Lady Simtal gave birth to his child she sent away to use as a trump card if she ever needed it. At first they are against burying the Mhybe in a sarcophagus, but as Hood and K’rul speak they convince them she will rest in a dreamworld.
Kruppe wins a knuckles game against Scorch and Leff, they owe him money
Scorch and Leff are in a crisis. Their last boss, Boc, just died and they took on a desperate job to hunt down people on a debtor’s list
Kruppe offers to help them find people on the list for 33% of the cut
Irilta carries Murillio and puts him on the counter
Kruppe tells Meese to go get Coll
Picker, Blend, Antsy, Bluepearl, Mallet, and Duiker gather at the longtable with Pearl and Antsy’s bloody swords on it
The meeting is filled with awkward silences
Bluepearl has a headache from using Mockra
Picker wonders two possibilities
The Assassin’s Guild put a contract on their heads
K’rul’s Bar is set up in an old temple, an old cult may want it back
Mallet says since they moved in, the ghosts have been moaning and begging for blood specifically spilled in the temple
Councillor Coll runs into the bar asking Mallet for his High Denul, not caring that he might be targeted by association
Mallet takes Bluepearl with him
Gardens of the Moon
After the Siege of Pale, Cpl. Picker and Sgt. Antsy found Cpt. Ganoes Paran’s body after being killed by Sorry

Mallet thinks Paran should be dead, helps look over and heal him. Mallet also heals Kalam’s wounds after the rooftop battle with the Guild assassins, Coll’s thigh wound after facing Adjunct Lorn (attacking anyone suspicious of following her). Mallet is repulsed by the Azath House forming from Raest’s acorn Finnest, as it was anathema to Denul. Mallet also confirms Apsalar is no longer possessed. Mallet’s worried about Whiskeyjack’s leg injured when a pillar collapsed on him.
Memories of Ice
While patrolling a smuggler’s route, Picker held up Munug and purchased three ivory torcs blessed by Treach from him. Once worn, she couldn’t remove them.
Picker and Blend helped steal Fiddler’s old card table from Caladan Brood’s tent.
While securing an alliance with the Whiteface Barghast, the torcs started burning Picker’s arm.
During the Siege of Capustan, Picker was glad to be able to give away the torcs the Gruntle, the Mortal Sword of Treach
Picker was suspicious of Paran’s connection to Silverfox, Antsy nearly attacks Paran for putting them in danger by keeping them in the dark, Mallet intervenes saying Paran’s isolated himself
After the siege, Bauchelain and Korbal Broach approached Picker for directions to a clothing shop, Picker found them rude and punched both of them unconscious
Cpt. Ganoes Paran promotes Picker from Corporal to Lieutenant to be his second-in-command of the Bridgeburners
During the Siege of Coral, Picker and the Bridgeburners fought their way to the keep fighting against undead K’Chain Che’Malle
During this siege, Trotts and Hedge die. Picker’s group coincidentally joins Lady Envy at the keep
Lady Envy’s easily able to kill the seerdomin, notes that Picker telling her they won’t take long fighting cost the Malazan soldiers lives
Picker helps inter the fallen in Moon’s Spawn
Dujek gives them a wagon full of money so they can retire
Picker and Blend purchase K’rul’s Belfry and converts it into a bar
Duiker is a friend to Heboric Light Touch, a Malazan priest of Fener and historian that was persecuted for writing a treasonous history accusing Laseen of murder and being a bad empress
Duiker comes to Hissar in Seven Cities to join the Malaz 7th Army led by Coltaine. Duiker and Kulp plotted to save their friend Heboric, as well as Felisin Paran.
While on the Chain of Dogs, the Trygalle Trade Guild were hired by Dujek Onearm and the cabal council of Darujhistan to deliver life-saving supplies to Coltaine and the refugees

Wondering how an outlaw could pull rank, Dujek told them ‘Never underestimate the Empress’ and ‘The Empress cannot lose such leaders such as Coltaine of the Crow Clan’, at this point Coltaine and Duiker knew the outlawry was a feint
Quick Ben also gave the Trygalle Trade Guild a ‘small oblong bottle of smoky gray glass on a silver chain’ to deliver to Coltaine, who rejected it and tossed it to Duiker
When Duiker was captured outside, Mallick Rel slapped Duiker to the ground and the bottle smashed against his chest
Baruk sent two familiars, Irp and Rudd, to retrieve the glass shards and Duiker’s body and take them back to Darujhistan
In the Memories of Ice epilogue, Duiker is in K’rul’s Tavern and tells the ‘dead’ Bridgeburners the story of Coltaine and the Chain of Dogs
High Alchemist Baruk reads through some books
The first book describes Anomander Rake and Osseric’s alliance falling out
Together as Children of Eleint they were hunting Draconus, Slayer of Eleint
Lady Spite ambushed him and knocked him out
Anomander vowed their alliance would end and they would be enemies
Baruk believes the Thousand Gods are fictional, created by Dillat who wrote Dark and Light
Another passage describes a war between the First Born dragons vs. the children dragons over accepting K’rul’s bargain
The war would not stop as long as the Gates of Starvald Demelain remained opened and unguarded
Osserick had cleansed Kurald Liosan of rivals, Soletaken, D’ivers, and feral purebloods to be the first Realm that sealed the Gate to Starvald Demelain
Baruk complains to Crone about the inaccuracies
Anomander thought Baruk would be amused by Dillat’s work. Anomander has whole rooms cramped with trash books because he finds them amusing
Crone notices Baruk has been subpar as a host
Baruk’s been troubled by a lot of things, for example the Rhivi people saying the White Face Barghast have completely disappeared almost immediately after the fall of Coral
Crone explains the White Face Barghast left to the seas, and the Grey Swords went to Elingarth and purchased ships to follow them
Crone knows this is a distraction
Baruk feels his cordial relations to Anomander Rake is ending, not because he did anything wrong but because of Tiste Andii chronic ennui
He’s worried Rake will stop talking to him because of depression
Baruk asks Crone if Rake can reconsider opening diplomatic relations between Darujhistan and Black Coral, the council is prepared to send delegates and construct an embassy
Crone laughs, it’s the same estate crushed by a Soletaken demon
Baruk gets nervous when Crone doesn’t have an answer
Crone barrages him with more questions which makes Baruk even more anxious
Chillbais flies through the window screaming ‘Out!’
Both Chillbais and Crone are disgusted by the other person
Baruk let’s Crone stay the night and sends Chillbais away to give him more work later
[Note: Chillbais says something got out of the Azath House]

(Gardens of the Moon) Baruk is an alchemist and leader of the T’orrud Cabal, mages and secret rulers of Darujhistan. Anomander Rake visited and allied with Baruk, with Darujhistan being the last standing free city on Genabackis. Baruk’s priority was protecting Oponn’s coin-bearer and slaying them if the Lord pushed bad luck. Knowing the Malazans aimed for Raest’s barrow, he sends Kruppe and the Phoenix Inn regulars to investigate while protecting the coin-bearer, Crokus.

Rake visits a second time, revealing he started the internal war of the Assassin’s Guild to prevent the Malazans from contracting them to kill Baruk. Baruk is pissed because the Guild is vital to facilitating unavoidable bloodshed between council members.
Baruk takes Rake to Lady Simtal’s Gedderone’s Eve Fete for the potential to meet the other powerful factors in Darujhistan.

The Bridgeburners make contact with Vorcan and she accepts the contract to kill the T’orrud Cabal. Vorcan swiftly eliminated 3 cabal mages, was nearly able to kill Baruk but was thwarted by Tiste Andii assassin Serrat and Crokus who knocked Vorcan unconscious by throwing bricks at her.

(Deadhouse Gates & Memories of Ice) Baruk and the T’orrud Cabal hired the Trygalle Trade Guild to deliver food and water to the Chain of Dogs. Baruk also crafted a smoky bottle necklace intending to resurrect Coltaine should he die, which instead brought Duiker back to life in Darujhistan.
Endest Silann is a retired High Mage of the Tiste Andii, presently works as the castellan for the New Andiian Palace
Feels like he retired from the military with PTSD and is unable to adjust to civilian life or be content with it
Muses on Black Coral
Silanah rests motionless for a year, on the northwest tower of the palace. The citizens think she’s a statue

Kurald Galain had truly manifested around Black Coral and Coral Bay, otherworldly beings lurk under the waters and sunk a fishing trawler. Endest is forced to order cadaver eels from a new food supplier as a result
The streets of the Outwater Market of the Fish District are so crowded, wagons can’t fit and have to be parked in a lot north of Grey Hill
Endless streams of porters from Cart Square weaving in and out of foot traffic
The Andiian District lies south of Grey Hill, much less populated. No one’s hanging out on their front steps talking to neighbors or passers by
The Tiste Andii on the street ignore Endest more than usual, he wonders if it’s because of his old age
Endest remembers fondly of when he was young, first stepping into the mortal world with Anomander Rake
Endest walks up the street past the rubble of the old palace, traumatic memories and a pressure headache
Recalls Rake asked Endest, as his last High Mage, to hide Moon’s Spawn under the ocean
Hiding under the sea caused irreparable damage to both Moon’s Spawn and Endest. Endest felt sympathetic pain as Moon’s Spawn was internally collapsing under the water pressure
Endest Silann lost his power as a High Mage after it was finished, thinks he should’ve died with the sky keep
Now Endest is a manager of a palace, making schedules, making sure the kitchen and hearth is stocked
Wonders if Rake can show him gratitude for such mundane tasks
Spinnock Durav wins a five-hour long game of kef tanar against Seerdomin and three others in the Scour Tavern
Spinnock is a big burly Tiste Andii, had black hair with the fainted tinge of red, and wide set eyes
Seerdomin, a man that still held onto the title he was served under the Pannion Domin in Coral Keep
Kef Tanar is a Tiste Andii game based on the succession wars of Mother Dark’s First Children
It was a tile game that can be played for a pot among multiple players
Motifs of Light Dark Shadow
It’s like a weird mix of miniature war-gaming, chess, and Magic the Gathering using tiles and dice rolls
Spinnock has 20,000 years of experience. He’s very old
Spinnock buys a pitcher for everyone
Spinnock is surprised people are still willing to live here without sunlight
Seerdomin talks about how he welcomes the eternal night that Kurald Galain brings to Black Coral, people can also easily ride or sail a short trip to see the sun again
Tiste Andii knows when its daytime even in darkness
Spinnock likes Seerdomin as a friend. Despite Seerdomin seeming to have more trauma than Tiste Andii, appears to be a human trait that keeps him resilient and holds despair back.
Spinnock feels like a parasite feeding off Seerdomin’s energy, spending quality time with Seerdomin is what keeps Spinnock living
Seerdomin has a new habit of going on hikes to look at the ocean
Weeks ago, he’s regularly seen Anomander Rake at noon time also looking at the ocean
Spinnock says his court are all either dead or missing
Korlat, Orfantal, Sorrit, Pra’iran
With no threat of war against Black Coral, it feels strange for Anomander Rake to just be a bureaucrat. Seerdomin wonders if he’s chafing at his duties
Spinnock doesn’t know, was never apart of Rake’s inner circle and last spoke to him centuries ago
Spinnock jokes he wasn’t really suited as a commander, got lost in the Mott Woods for five days. Hopes the alcohol doesn’t expose that he told Seerdomin half-truths and outright lies
Spinnock and Seerdomin schedule their next game and silently bid each other farewell

cards.h: Scene 3 (Forest by the Sea, Nimander Golit)

i.html: Nimander Golit, Skintick, Aranatha, Desra, Nenanda, and Kedeviss follow Clip through Kurald Galain
The Tiste Andii exit into a forest by the sea, sunrise
Nimander’s cousin Skintick pulls him to the side to talk about how he doesn’t trust Clip
Skintick jokes about Clip claiming the titles of Herald of Mother Dark and Mortal Sword. Skintick would rather walk away and go anywhere else.
Want to tell Clip he’s a fool in a subtle way, ‘The forest does not change’
The phrase triggers Nimander and makes him remember the deaths of his unnamed lover, Andarist, and Phaed
Skintick thinks they earned the right to join the community of Tiste Andii following Rake
Nimander agrees, their goal is to follow Clip just long enough to join that community
Aranatha, another cousin, joins Nimander and Skintick
Was listening to Nenanda asking Clip questions. Clip said they were met with “layers of resistance”, they ended up more south than he intended or hoped
Nimander, Skintick, and Aranatha hike up a cliff and have a view of the ocean, no beaches or villages
They go back to the group

(House of Chains, though unnamed at the time) Nimander is the first son of Anomander Rake. He was one among many Tiste Andii, led by Rake’s older brother Andarist, that defended the Throne of Shadow on Drift Avalii. Nimander’s unnamed lover died in the assault.
(Bonehunters) After Andarist was killed by the Tiste Edur, Traveller was determined to become the sole protector of the throne and sent the Malazans he came with and the surviving Tiste Andii away.

A Jakatakan fleet picked up the Malazans Nimander’s kin when they were stranded for months at sea. They were dropped off at Malaz Isle during the fall of the jade suns. They end up at Coop’s Hanged Man Inn. Withal, last seen being rescued by Mael/Bugg from the Crippled God’s realm, is also present at the inn. Adjunct Tavore sends Bottle to find Withal and bring him back, T’amber created the doll to find him. Withal is brought over, his Tiste Andii wife Sandalath Drukorlat became a motherly figure to Nimander’s kin so they were brought along as well.
(Reaper’s Gale)
Nimander’s kin were on Tavore’s ship, the Froth Wulf, for a year until they arrived at Second Maiden Fort in the Letherii Empire. His

daughter/sister (Erikson couldn’t decide which, but her mother is definitely Lady Envy) Phaed is a psychopath hated Sandalath and vowed to kill her. Nimander didn’t sleep for days, waiting for Phaed to move her move, and strangled her right as she tried to stab Sandalath in the middle of the night. When Sandalath left the room to talk to Tavore and the other Malazans, Withal threw Phaed out the window, reassures Nimander that he’ll assume all responsibility to he doesn’t feel guilty, and tells everyone it’s an accident.
After the Malazans left Nimander’s kin on the island, Clip appears claiming to be Mother Dark’s Herald to take them all to their father, Anomander Rake.
Clip assesses the Drift Avalii survivors to find which he could groom
Nimander was too sensitive, the type the realities of the world crushes with its brutality
Skintick reminded Clip of himself, a smartass. However he lacked the vicious core to do what’s necessary
Kedeviss an anxious woman like Nimander that Clip predicted would die sooner than later
Aranatha is an anxious child
Nenanda is a young man with rage burning inside of him, Clip thinks he’d the best candidate to groom
Desra is an ambitious, ruthless, and attractive woman that Clip also wants at his side
With Nimander, Skintick, and Aranatha gone and the rest asleep, Clip holds out his chain with rings at each end
Miniature portals would open and close as the rings spin around each other
The mages of Andara all used their power to enchant the chain with ritual magic and their own souls, leaving them vulnerable to a massacre by the Letherii
Clip feels like he’s the hero in a chosen one trope, spins the chain to mimic the cries of souls trapped inside

(Reaper’s Gale) Clip is a 19 year old Bluerose Tiste Andii that lived in the monastery Andara within the Bluerose Mountains, ruled by five Tiste Andii wizards that formed the Onyx Order. By their command, Clip retrieved Silchas Ruin and his companions to the monastery. After the Onyx Order spoke with Silchas Ruin, they named Clip the Mortal Sword of the Black Winged Lord (Anomander Rake) who would guide Silchas Ruin to find Scabandari’s soul.

When the Letherii Patriotists slaughtered all of the Bluerose Tiste Andii within the monastery, the Onyx Wizards died on an altar sanctified to the Hold of Darkness, which let Clip use his spinning chain to open a portal into Kurald Galain, which took them to Starvald Demelain, then finally the Refugium cave guarded by Trull Sengar, Onrack, and Onrack’s son Ulshun Pral who possessed Scabandari’s finnest in the form of a flint dagger (which presumably Gothos gave to him). Clip killed Fear Sengar who tried to protect his brother, then Trull beat his ass forcing him to flee through one of the gates in the Refugium cave.

Silchas Ruin made a deal with the Azath Tower that he would deliver the Azath’s seed (Kettle) to the Refugium and stab Scabandari’s finnest dagger into Kettle to form an Azath House. The Refugium was a dream world within Omtose Phellack where flesh-and-blood Imass lived trapped in time before the Ritual of Tellann. There is a cave that contained twelve gates leading to the other warrens. When Silchas Ruin completed his mission with Clip’s guidance, the Azath House formed from Kettle anchored the Refugium into reality and sealed the twelve gates.
Clip later appears on Second Maiden Fort to retrieve Nimander’s kin with the intent to find Anomander Rake.
Spinnock Durav walks from Scour Tavern to the New Andiian Palace to speak to Anomander Rake
Passes by the ruins of Coral Keep
Passed under Silanah, unnerved because he’s seen her power several times.
The last was at Mott Wood, her breath killing Crimson Guard and Mott Irregulars like killing ants with an ax
Crimson Guard mage Cowl retaliating with sorcery that wounded Silanah and made her retreat
Despite a stoic exterior, Rake’s eyes were enraged as he hunted Cowl for hurting Silanah
Unclear who fled away, but Cowl was seen in Darujhistan after their battle
Remembers when Silanah fought Raest with five other Tiste Andii eleint soletaken
Spinnock felt nervous by the alliance between the Tiste Andii and dragons
Rake initially warred with the pure blood dragons, dragons that stopped serving K’rul to obtain power for themselves
It’s still a mystery to Spinnock why Rake fought the dragons and how Silanah became his partner
Spinnock enters the New Andiian Palace
The palace never had guards, 15 people live in the palace
Through the arched entrance, up the flagstone ramp, through another archway that opened into a huge dome with 28 spiraling black-silver terondai of Mother Dark. Commissioned by Anomander Rake
The terondai dome would be the closest thing to Kurald Galain’s heart in this manifestation on Coral
Two human servants are scrubbing the floor because they’re bored and have nothing else to do
Spinnock walks up a bone-white staircase across the dome chamber to the elongated room facing the ocean, finds Anomander here
Anomander asks about his warhammer chess game
Spinnock reports on his mission to Assail. He had to fight and kill countless for 3 miles to the shore. However, the situation is self-contained and doesn’t think Rake needs to go to Assail
Though traumatized, Spinnock is eager to serve to fulfill a destiny he learned about himself
Unseen by anyone. Deed unwitnessed. Heroic efforts earning naught but one man’s gratitude
Meanwhile Anomander is trying to raise his spirits, make Spinnock rest during his vacation to not collapse under the pressure he put himself in
‘A weapon must be used, Lord, lest it rust’
‘A weapon overused, Spinnock, grows blunted, notched’
‘Perhaps, then, Lord, such a weapon must be put away. A new one found’
‘That time is yet to arrive, Spinnock Durav’
Spinnock departs and passes by Endest Silann in the hall, excited about finding a new vendor for eels
Seerdomin is at a street food shop, eavesdropping on a conversation between Bucch, Harak, and a third man
All are drinking Bastion kelyk, a pungent brew rising in popularity in Black Coral
Someone has been organizing the people to kill the Tiste Andii for the Darkness to go away, Bucch had been recruited
Half the humans in Black Coral were soldiers in the Pannion Domin, and the Tiste Andii did not confiscate any of their armor or weapons
The trio leave to the next meeting
Seerdomin follows them
Silanah watches all of the activity in Black Coral, but she also sees beyond Kurald Galain’s Darkness
Outside of Black Coral, pilgrims set up campfires all along a serpentine route
The pilgrims come with offerings to bring to the Great Barrow of the Redeemer
Sea shells, polished stones, raw copper, jewelry, gem studded scabbards, rare silk, Delantine linen, Darujhistan coins, loot from battlefield corpses, locks of hair from relatives or heroes
Silanah recalls a Rhivi prayer
A man who stirs awake the serpent is a man without fear. A man without fear has forgotten the rules of life
Silanah believes the mortals did forget, and needed reminding
Morning in Darujhistan
Kruppe is stuffing his face with pastries and spiced apples. Until he chokes and coughs up pie, landing on poor hungover Meese’s face
Sulty comes in to wipe her clean as she stares deathly at Kruppe
A Trygalle Trade Guild carriage suddenly appears on a street next to Quip’s Bar and crash lands into a shop
In the carriage’s wake, human bodies or body parts are scattered all over the street, some parts twitching
Shareholders Faint, Glanno Tarp, Reccanto Ilk, Sweetest Sufferance, and Master Quell all get up and grab a table at Quip’s Bar
Quip Younger, who inherited the bar from his dad, used to have a crush on Faint
Kruppe sloshes his mouth with expensive wine and spits it on the floor, pissing off Meese
Mallet comes downstairs, drinks a cup of wine, says Murillio will be alright but can’t dance for a couple of weeks. His ‘funk’ may delay or worsen it however
Kruppe sent Bluepearl home earlier
Kruppe promises he’ll find who put out a contract on the ex-soldiers
Mallet leaves, Bluepearl is at the door waiting for him
Meese wonders if assassins from the up-and-running Malazan embassy is responsible
Kruppe is confident Darujhistan Assassin’s Guild is responsible
Kruppe reaches into his pouch to pay his tab but he’s broke
Scorch and Leff wait at a quayside, Leff hopes they can catch their target debtor, Brokul, on the assumption this is how people flee the city
Leff eats a conch, Scorch is disgusted by any meat without blood
Fishers are pulling their sliverfish catch in
Children run around hoping to get paid to help tie up the fish for the fish market
Grey backed Gadrobi cats, thousands of feral generations, kill the gulls attempting to steal sliverfish
Old women used pokers to collect sliverfish that dropped out of the netting
The women would also fight each other if there were few fish
Scorch remembers his grandmother having scars from the pokers
Gruntle returns to Darujhistan through south Worrytown with four carriages
The beggars surround him, one climbs up and pulls back the hood of a driver revealing that the driver, Gisp, is dead. All four of the drivers are dead, but still drove the carriages to follow Gruntle
Gruntle brandishes his iron cutlasses, both marked with black and pale orange tiger stripes. Gruntle has tiger stripes tattooed all over his body, feline eyes, and
The beggars scream and flee, three crows land on Gisp’s head and shoulders and eat his face
Gruntle arrived at Sirik’s estate, Sirik stands surrounded by 6 private bodyguards including the scar-faced captain, Kest
Gruntle was hired by Sirik to obtain and deliver Bastion kelyk. Only was able to retrieve half.
Gruntle had warned Sirik he didn’t hire enough people, as a result 16 people died after 100 Dwell raiders attacked, Gruntle is the sole survivor
Gruntle demands his full payment, or else he’ll have Sirik blacklisted from using the [Caravanserai] Guild’s services
Sirik pays Gruntle
Still morning, Gruntle heads home
Gruntle expects a self-proclaimed High Priestess of Trake of a local temple and other Trake worshippers to be waiting outside his house, desperately seeking his attention
Gruntle considers them losers, though believes the priestess can sense his battle cry even 30 leagues (about 90 miles) away
Gruntle does not enjoy fighting or killing, still regrets the loss of his friends
[Note: Harllo who died and Stonny who was traumatized]
Gruntle decides to avoid the main streets, or else any little bump will make him lose his temper and kill people around him
His path through the alleys takes him to a Trygalle Trade Guild carriage in the Lakefront District
Gruntle has heard the Trygalle Trade Guild is a competitor that pays much more than the Caravanserai Guild
As he walked by the Trygalle’s horse, Gruntle was amazed it was indifferent and not spooked by his presence
Gruntle thinks about owning a horse like that, or a dead one. Then remembers discovering his new ability to command the dead
Torvald Nom has returned to Darujhistan, rowing his round coracle paddleboat, nearly crushed between two trader boats, and abandons it among crayfish traps
Torvald wears a floppy sealskin hat, and a combination of leather under armour garb and Nathii fisherman garb. Carries an odd scimitar with a snake pommel with empty sockets where gems were
Also wears a Moranth cape with items handled carefully in the pockets
Torvald is immediately is caught by Scorch and Leff in an alley, they have history together
Torvald claims their partnership was officially absolved and disappointed that they are desperate enough to work Lender Gareb’s debt list
Torvald claims Gareb only bought him dinner and pitchers of drink once, which inflated to a debt of a thousand silver councils
Torvald convinces them to give him one night to clear his debts and help them with the debtor list
After the Malazan Empire conquered northern Genabackis, Torvald Nom became a bandit leader until he was captured by the Malazan Ashok Regiment and became a prisoner under Master Silgar at Silverlake
Torvald Nom became friends with Karsa Orlong and joined him when he made his escape attempt
Both separated, but were captured again and put on a ship to the otataral mines in Seven Cities
Torvald Nom nursed Karsa while he was chained, helping Karsa survive and keep his sanity
The Seven Faces in the Rock/Unbound T’lan Imass had pulled their ship into the flooded Nascent realm, Torvald risked his life to keep Karsa from drowning
Karsa and Torvald made a deal to rescue their slavemaster Silgar in exchange for his mage companion to open a warren that put them on the Seven Cities coast
Karsa and Torvald spent some time with the Keeper until they departed for Ehrlitan
Master Silgar and Arak tribesman captures Karsa and Torvald (a third time)
Torvald lights a fire to attract a rival Gral tribe, Torvald’s throat is slit and left behind
Off screen, the Gral tribe saved Torvald’s life and took him to Ehrlitan where Torvald made contact with his Nom family in the city
Torvald led his new Gral and Nom allies to break into the Malazan compound to rescue Karsa Orlong and Leoman
Once successful, Torvald parted ways and invites Karsa to visit him to his hometown of Darujhistan one day
Humble Measure is the 27 year old business owner of the Eldra Iron Mongers company that produces iron in Darujhistan
Humble Measure’s father was the 12th generation owner of the Eldra Iron Mongers and operated in One Eye Cat
Purchased a Rhivi woman slave and gave birth to Humble Measure as a bastard son
The father attempted to conspire with the Malazan conquest of One Eye Cat in exchange for ensured wealth, was caught and killed
Humble Measure witnessed the rape and murder of his mother and half sisters
Humble Measure and the household staff was tortured until rescued by Jorrick Sharplance, a mercenary company leader
After the Malazan succeeded in their second attempt in conquering One Eye Cat, Jorrick evacuated the prisoners to Old King Lake
Humble Measure led his household survivors to Pale, until the Malazan Siege of Pale forced them further south to Darujhistan

Humble Measure took over the Eldra Iron Monger office in Darujhistan, earned the loyalty of the household survivors who remained with him, and pledged to protect Darujhistan against further Malazan conquest
The vaults underneath the complex contained records going back 600 years
Humble Measure made a secret office in the vaults with protective wards where he worked tirelessly
The single servant who knew about the vaults delivered a wax message reporting that four assassins of the Assassin’s Guild had died and failed Humble Measure’s contract against the ex-Bridgeburners
Lady Spite’s beauty and crew of bhokarala made her entrance into Darujhistan’s docks newsworthy to spread all over town
Lady Spite wore a flowing diaphanous emerald green blouse, a black leather with three knives, tight tanned leather breeches and rawhide leggings
The bhokarala were chaotic yet deftly docked the ship, placed the gangplank onto the pier, and hissed at the dock clerk coming to extract the mooring fee
Lady Spite walks into the captain’s cabin

Lady Spite was one of the twelve Nameless Ones that summoned Dejim Nebrahl and made a deal for Dejim to attack Mappo and Icarium, then veered to fly off as Dejim killed the eleven remaining Nameless Ones
Lady Spite visited Mappo (rescued by Iskaral Pust) after Dejim succeeded in separating him from Icarium, claiming she was banished from the Nameless Ones
Lady Spite offers to help Mappo find Icarium. Mappo and Iskaral Pust boards her ship to sail on the Otataral Sea
At sea, Lady Spite spoke to the Eres’al who had to depart and leave them vulnerable
When the Jade Suns rained onto the planet, Lady Spite veered into an eleint and rescued Crokus and Scillara from a nearby ship while Barathol Mekhar and Chaur also climbed onto her ship
In the cabin room sits Crokus Younghand, Scillara, Iskaral Pust, his donkey, Mogora, Mappo, Barathol Mekhar, and Chaur
Lady Spite plans to disembark at dusk, Crokus is impatient and wants to warn his friends in the city
Spite recommends Mappo travel to Lamatath to find a ship and sail to Lether
Mogora divines that Iskaral will fight his nemesis here and restore balance
Spite does not believe Shadow can impose balance on anything, thinks [Shadowthrone] is a diabolical, unpleasant god
Barathol Mekhar plans to explore the city with Chaur
Spite senses “alarming personages” in the city and wants to think alone

cards.h: ** Crokus Younghand and Apsalar (Gardens of the Moon)

i.html: A simple fishergirl was possessed by Cotillion and Rigga the Seer, a wax witch, before the slaughter of Itko Kan
Rigga the Seer was grieving her family lost in war, foresaw Apsalar’s possession and thus wanted to protect her
Shadowthrone and Cotillion wanted revenge for their deaths, planned to use her for the Empire’s downfall
She enlisted under the name Sorry and was attached to the Bridgeburners
In Darujhistan, the mischievous god Oponn gifted Crokus Younghand a coin which made him a target by several people, including Sorry, who did not want Oponn disrupting any of their plans
Right before attacking Crokus, Anomander Rake threatened Shadowthrone with Dragnipur to stop his schemes in Darujhistan and thus ended Sorry’s possession
Rigga the Seer’s protection kept Sorry’s mind from shattering
Crokus Younghand takes Sorry back to the city and gives her the name Apsalar, after the Lady of Thieves
Crokus was swept up in the events in the Malazan conflicts against Darujhistan.
His uncle Mammot was possessed by the Jaghut Tyrant Raest and was killed
Tasked by Anomander Rake to protect Alchemist Baruk, knocked the assassin Vorcan unconscious with two bricks which saved Baruk’s life
Once the conflict was over, the Bridgeburners (then outlawed) had found Sorry. Realizing she is no longer possessed and feeling pity for her, Kalam and Fiddler decide to take her home to Itko Kan.
Crokus decides to tag along
Fiddler and Kalam found an opportunity to take revenge against Empress Laseen for their annihilation at the Siege of Pale and their outlawry.

Decided to detour to Seven Cities. Kalam would initiate the Whirlwind Rebellion while Fiddler takes Crokus and Apsalar to find the Tremorlor, an Azath House, somewhere on the continent that connects to the Deadhouse, an Azath House in Malaz City.
As a backup plan, they wanted to use Apsalar’s skills gained by Cotillion to have her assassinate Laseen
Fiddler, Crokus, and Apsalar are attacked by soletaken and d’ivers, but are saved by Icarium and Mappo Runt
They are very friendly and take them to Tesem Temple, a temple of Shadow inhabited by Iskaral Pust
Most likely from Shadowthrone and Cotillion’s schemes, Apsalar’s father Rellock had been sent to Iskaral Pust as his servant.

Iskaral made a deal with Rellock, to spare his and Apsalar’s lives and restore his missing arm, in exchange for planting false trails leading the soletaken and d’ivers away from the Path of Hands to be trapped by the Azath House, Tremorlor
Iskaral tried to make Apsalar become Sha’ik Reborn and trap Icarium in Tremorlor, which both failed
The group fought their way to Tremorlor, only Crokus, Apsalar, Rellock, and Fiddler were transported to the Deadhouse in Malaz City
They reunite with Kalam, who had spoken to Empress Laseen and gave up his plan to kill her
Apsalar requests Shadowthrone to take her, her father, and Crokus back to her home in Itko Kan and sever all ties between them and the gods

cards.h: ** Crokus Younghand and Apsalar (House of Chains)

i.html: Apsalar’s father, Rellock, passed away as soon as they returned home to Itko Kan. Cotillion gives them a job to sail to Drift Avalii to confirm if Tiste Edur are attempting to take the Throne of Shadow
On the island, they help Rake’s brother Andarist, Tiste Andii grandchildren, stranded Malazans, and Traveller defend the throne against a Tiste Edur attack
Andarist and the stranded Malazans die, Traveller takes up his sword Vengeance the duty to guard the Throne of Shadow
Cotillion then tasks and transports Crokus and Apsalar to Tesem Temple for a task, yet unspecified
Apsalar bargains with Cotillion to stop making Crokus a killer and leaves to be his servant
Cotillion grants Crokus the duty to be Felisin Younger’s next guardian
Crokus was tasked by Cotillion to defend Heboric, Scillara, and Felisin Younger on their way to the Jade statue in Otataral Island
They are attacked by the Unbound T’lan Imass to prevent Heboric from reaching the Jade Statue and kidnap Felisin Younger
Crokus and Scillara are rescued by Barathol. Together they decide to bury Heboric’s body at the Jade Statue, then sail back home to Darujhistan
An event similar to the Fall of the Crippled God occurs, Heboric’s proximity to the Jade Statue triggers huge jade arms and domes to protect the world from the falling suns
Crokus, Scillara, Barathol, and Chaur meet up with Mappo and they sail to Darujhistan
(Deadhouse Gates)
Mappo Runt had traveled with Icarium for over 200 years, keeping watch over him and making sure Icarium does not recover his memories and keep his rage in check.

While traveling the Pan’potsun Odhan, they get involved with the Path of Hands (something that would allow the victorious soletaken or d’ivers to ascend) and discover its gate within Tesem, a Temple of Shadow with Iskaral Pust as its priest
Mappo and Icarium join Crokus, Apsalar, and Rellock in diverting the soletaken and d’ivers away from the Path of Hands, instead into to be funneled and trapped into the Azath House, Tremorlor
After entering the House, Mappo and Icarium are transported to Aren Way after the Army of the Apocalypse defeated and crucified the Chain of Dogs
Mappo rescues the Hengese lap dog Roach and Wickan cattle dog Bent
Icarium forgets the entire sequence of Deadhouse Gates and they wander off westward into the Jhag Odhan
(House of Chains)
Mappo and Icarium met Karsa Orlong when he left Raraku to find a Jhag Horse for himself
Icarium was excavating a cave containing a statue of a seven-headed hound
Karsa faintly recognized Icarium’s names in the caves of the Laederon Plateau and Icarium recognized Karsa as Teblor, calling his tribes fallen
Icarium shatters Karsa’s ironwood sword, Karsa punches Icarium’s face KO’ing him, and Mappo bonks Karsa with his club KO’ing him
(Bonehunters)
The Nameless Ones summon Dejim Nebrahl, an ancient terror that is a d’ivers whose form is several t’rohlbahl (scaled panther)

Dejim Nebrahl attacks Mappo and Icarium, separating them. His original objective is complete, and then gets hunted down by Deragoth that Ganoes Paran released to specifically hunt and killed Dejim Nebrahl

Icarium is found by Taralack Veed, a Nameless One agent who gaslights Icarium into believing he’s a companion and guides him to be taken by the Tiste Edur and travel to Letheras to slay Emperor Rhulad

Mappo is found by Lady Spite and Iskaral Pust who decides to help him reunite with Icarium. Mogora helps heal him with Ardata’s power. Later after the fall of the suns, they meet up and join with Crokus’ group

Mappo Runt’s elders performed a ritual which summoned the Nameless Ones. Mappo is named as a ‘chosen warrior’ to be Icarium’s guardian. They told him that Icarium had destroyed his home village that became a trader town
The Nameless Ones were the left hand of the First Empire (human), with another sect being the right hand
When entering the maze of roots that led to Tremorlor, corpses of the Nameless Ones littered the floor
Icarium has memories of the Nameless Ones telling him he should never travel alone, and remembers various faces of different partners throughout history. The Nameless Ones make him lose his memory
Dancer and Kellanved has ordered the Talon to kill all Nameless Ones because they resented them for entering the Azath Deadhouse in Malaz City
Gothos, Icarium’s father, reveals to Mappo that the Nameless Ones had destroyed Mappo’s home, not Icarium
(Reaper’s Gale)
Taralack Veed continues to be the Nameless One’s appointed guardian to Icarium, as they are guests on the Tiste Edur ship bringing back champions to kill Emperor Rhulad
Upon arrival, several buildings including Scale House collapse in an earthquake
Icarium seems to have been in Lether in the far past
Icarium is a god to the Cabalhii monks
Icarium actually doesn’t do much besides walk around the city. Meets Karsa Orlong and assures that he has no reason to fight Rhulad

Suddenly towards the end of the novel, Icarium walks to the nexus point. In the far past, Icarium had built a gigantic machine that seems to span the entire city. As Icarium spills his own blood, the entire city quakes and white fire as powerful as lasers converge on Icarium like he’s the focal point
Cliffhanger on what the machine actually is
(House of Chains)
Scillara was the daughter of a Malazan Ashok Regiment soldier who abandoned her and her mother

She became one of Bidithal’s spies within Korbolo Dom’s Dogslayer army (traitorous Malazans), a victim of Bidithal’s female genital mutilation, drug abuse, rape, two abortions, and pregnant at the time of the novel
Scillara was exposed as a spy and ordered to be murdered

As Scillara was being raped in an alley, she kills her rapist. The second rapist draws her further into the alley. Heboric appears and kills him with his jade tiger claw, then uses his power to heal Scillara’s durhang COPD-lungs and genital mutilation
Heboric takes Scillara to a temple and fully embraces his role as Treach’s Destriant
L’oric sent Scillara, Heboric, and Felisin Younger with Greyfrog to Tesem Temple
(Bonehunters)
Scillara travels with Crokus, Heboric, Greyfrog, and Felisin Younger to Otataral Island for Heboric’s mission
Health improves over time
When the Unbound T’lan Imass attack to kidnap Felisin Younger, Scillara is stabbed in the chest
Scillara recovers in Barathol’s village. Healed by L’oric’s Denul magic and gives birth to a Napan baby
L’oric tries to convince her to keep the baby, but she leaves it with Barathol’s villagers that are happy to raise them
Scillara becomes fwb’s with Crokus, can’t wait to start a new life with new friends in Darujhistan
While on a ship sailing to deliver Heboric’s body to the Otataral Island, the Jade Giants fall
Lady Spite as a dragon rescues them and together they sail to Darujhistan

(Deadhouse Gates) Iskaral Pust is the High Priest of Shadow within Tesem Temple, with an entourage of bhokarala and his trusty mule. The Path of Hands is possibly a Hold with a throne related to the Beast Throne, the soletaken or d’ivers would achieve Ascendancy if they obtained it. It was hidden within Tesem Temple and Iskaral Pust sent his servant Rellock to plant a false trail that leads the shapeshifters into a trap, in which the Azath House Tremorlor would imprison them. Iskaral planned to use Rellock (Apsalar’s father) as bait for Apsalar to become Sha’ik Reborn and for Icarium to also be trapped in Tremorlor. However, Felisin became Sha’ik Reborn and Shadowthrone failed to bargain with the Azath to take Icarium. Iskaral follows the group into Tremorlor and eventually returns home.

(House of Chains) Kalam was tasked by Cotillion to find the threat against Shadowthrone, delivers dusky diamonds that summon Azalan demons to Iskaral Pust. Iskaral then uses Shadow to drop Kalam off so he can infiltrate the Whirlwind. After the climax, Iskaral safely escorts Heboric, Scillara, Crokus, Felisin Younger, and Greyfrog to Tesem Temple.

(Bonehunters) After Mappo was defeated by Dejim Nebrahl, Iskaral rides out to save him. On the way there, Iskaral runs into Dejim Nebrahl and actually kicks its ass. With Mogora’s sorcery, Mappo is healed. Cotillion helps Mappo’s efforts to reunite with Icarium. Iskaral escorts him to the coast where they encounter Lady Spite and board her ship. After the Fall of the Jade Giants, they rescue Crokus, Scillara, Barathol, and Chaur and continue on their way to Darujhistan.
Barathol is Kalam’s distant cousin and was a former Red Blade, Seven Cities natives that were loyal to the Malazan Empire.

During Emperor Kellanved’s reign, Barathol killed the Malazan Fist of Aren (unknown why) and he was crucified. This both made the Red Blades more zealous to cover up their shame, while the Seven Cities natives were inspired to rebel in Barathol’s name. The Logros T’lan Imass were sent to put down the rebellion and slaughtered its people. Barathol had opened the city gates to escape, many people saw this as him opening the gates for the T’lan Imass to enter (which Barathol doesn’t understand because they could easily bypass as dust-shifting skeletons).

Ever since, Barathol was a respected smith in the quiet Tapur Crossroads Village. The Unbound T’lan Imass had appeared outside the village without taking action, making Barathol paranoid that they were coming for him. After the Unbound killed Heboric and kidnapped Felisin Younger, the villagers rescue the survivors in which L’oric visits soon after. A villager convinces Barathol to leave with Crokus and Scillara because once L’oric leaves and spreads worth that Barathol is alive he’ll be hunted down for his crimes at Aren. With Chaur, they all leave, find a boat that gets wrecked during the Fall of the Jade Giants, and are rescued by Lady Spite.
(Barathol Mekhar)
Barathol and Chaur follows Mappo to his makeshift room, seeing all of his belongings already packed up
Barathol offers to help Mappo find Icarium, Mappo declines not wanting to put them in harm's way. Mappo plans to travel a path different than Spite’s suggestion
Barathol wonders what to do with his life, having been a former Red Blade soldier
Mappo believes the skills of warriors are always in demand in Darujhistan to guard estates and merchant caravans
Mappo hugs Chaur, who tries to dance with him
Barathol and Mappo bid each other farewell
(Iskaral Pust)
Iskaral Pust and Mogora incoherently argue
In their bed area, Scillara asks if Crokus wants her to come with him
Crokus doesn’t hesitate to say yes, believes she’ll like meeting his friends at the Phoenix Inn
Scillara decides to let Crokus reunite with his old life by himself for the first night
Inside she believes there was no love between them, only convenient sex
Scillara does not want to embarrass Crokus with having an “overweight, pipe-sucking ex-whore at his side”
Spending time with Crokus absorbed his insecurity, not a good quality to have when exploring a big city
Scillara decided to join Barathol exploring the city during the Fete and heads up
On the deck of the ship, she sees Barathol making his way to appease the town guard, wishing to avoid Lady Spite’s wrath unleashing over a misunderstanding about mooring fees
Scillara walks over ready to pay with her own coin
Rallick Nom is kicked in the head by Raest because “it seemed the thing to do”
Rallick’s poison on his weapons have lost their potency, but the otataral still is in his body
Vorcan, whom Raest calls a demon in truth and suggest is one of many names she’s had, had left
[Note: At this point you can guess this is the figure that Chillbais saw escape the Azath House]
The Master of the Deck [Ganoes Paran] had also visited and left
[Note: In Memories of Ice, Paran went into the Finnest House and learned he was Master of the Deck. In the epilogue, Paran moved in with Raest until Bonehunters]
Raest indirectly admits he will feel lonely with Rallick gone
Rallick thanks Raest for kicking him awake and walks out the door into the Darujhistan night

Rallick is a Phoenix Inn regular and a member of the Assassin’s Guild. He and Murillio conspired to kill Turban Orr in a duel and have Lady Simtal commit suicide, getting revenge on her for ruining Coll’s life and paving the way to put Coll back on the Darujhistan council. His clan leader Ocelot took an unsanctioned contract by Turban Orr to kill Coll. Rallick rubbed otataral dust on his skin which helped him kill Ocelot.

Adjunct Lorn planted Raest’s acorn-Finnest in a garden during Gedderone celebrations. As it grew into a wooden block, it became a meeting place between Vorcan, master of the Assassin’s Guild, and the Bridgeburners who made a contract to eliminate the T’orrud Cabal. Vorcan had him sit on the wooden block because the otataral dust on his skin slowed its growth. Baruk considers Rallick Nom a close friend, Rallick sent Crokus to go save Baruk. After Vorcan failed to kill Baruk and was being chased by Tiste Andii assassins (whom Rake ordered to protect Baruk), Rallick Nom brought her into the Finnest Azath House and they hibernate in the corridors to recover front their injuries.
Darujhistan continues to celebrate the new year with the Gedderone’s Fete
[Vorcan] wearing all black stands on a tower roof looking down upon the city, thinking about the future
[Rallick Nom] walks a street away from Coll’s estate, wondering if his reappearance would be wise to show his enemies
[Crokus] briskly walks to the Phoenix Inn
[Barathol, Chaur, and Scillara] walk up to the Gadrobi District night markets
[Iskaral Pust, Mogora, and the 20+ bhokarala] walk into the city
[Lady Spite] remains on the ship, wearing a loose black and crimson silk robe, looks on the city
[Humble Measure] writes another letter to the Assassin’s Guild then continues researching the ancient family literature
[Gruntle] drinks hot spiced wine, wincing at the sound of a child’s laughter in the next room
Torvald Nom approaches the new money estates of once-criminal moneylenders who purchased their rank
[Murillio] rests in the Phoenix Inn, dreaming of walking through a graveyard, mourning his youth
[Kruppe] eats pastries and looks at the door awaiting arrivals
Traveller tied himself to the tiller of a boat, and crashes it onto the black rocks along the Genabackan west coast, with corpses falling and sinking into the sea
Autumnal leaves rain down from the sky, despite no trees visible on the coastline
Traveller has dark skin, grew up in a savannah, average height, black kinked hair tied in braids, muscled
Wears a chain hauberk and has an ancient watermarked sword named Vengeance, made of two long strips of pale wood reinforced with blackened iron sheathed in a cracked scabbard
Among the leaves falling from the sky, a starving bear that wandered too far away from its inland home attacks Traveller
The bear bites the back of Traveller’s neck, cutting into his scalp and skull
Traveller elbows both sides of the bear’s head cutting its lip, heel-stomps its chest shattering its ribcage
Traveller reaches to pick up his sword on the ground and decapitates the bear
The bear’s blood boils on the blade of Vengeance, boils, turns black, then sheds in flakes
The sun starts to rise
Feeling that his head is bleeding all over, his rips his left shirt sleeve, folds it into a bandana, and ties it tightly around the torn skin and flesh of his head
Three days without water, Traveller cuts out the bear’s heart, squeezes it to drink the blood, then eats the heart
Walks inland to a wasteland of rocks, scrubs, ash, ravines, broken bedrock, jagged hills
To the north on his left, a grainy diffuse haze marred the sky above
Traveller can’t let himself die because he has forsaken Hood
‘In his wake, stripped branches spun and twisted down from the heaving clouds, plunging into the waves, as if torn from the moon itself.’

cards.h: Scene 2-1 (Forest by the Sea, Nimander Golit)

i.html: After walking across old tribal farmland, Nimander muses on the inevitable fall of civilization, time is the one true god
Skintick asks what’s got Nimander smiling like that, Nimander gets easily hurt by his words unintentionally
Desra says they should worship power, having enough earns you free will. Skintick believes free will is a delusion
Desra easily seduces men, allures them by becoming a mirror to feed men’s narcissism. She attempts this with Clip, but Nimander can see Clip is too obsessed with himself to fall victim
Nenanda takes the rear guard, is a boring wet blanket of a person that takes his duty too seriously and is too desperate for Clip’s approval
Nimander hears his unnamed lover in his head voicing her support
Phaed’s voice intrudes, wracking his mind with the guilt of her murder and lack of conviction
Phaed’s voice mentions writings of a Kharkanas woman in the Old Scrolls. Dark list, sadism, etc. The Tiste Andii including Andarist were afraid to speak of her, her name forbidden
The party finds a farm where fields of wrapped up corpses are staked above man-height purple colored, broad leafed plants. Dark fluids drips down from their noses onto the plants
The stream at the end of the farm has dark green, almost black water
Nimander quotes Andarist, ‘All possible cruelties are inevitable. All conceivable crimes has been committed’
Beyond the farmland is Morsko, an idyllic town set against a backdrop of low forested hills, people walk in the streets

cards.h: Scene 2-2 (Forest by the Sea, Nimander Golit)

i.html: A man approaches them. Long grey unkempt hair, burgundy robe, bare pale legs, comically large hands, black stains on hands and feet
The man is initially frustrated that they don’t speak the local language, welcomes them in broken Tiste Andii assuming they are traders from Black Coral
The townsfolk had black stains on their mouth, hands, and feet
The man says Bastion, Heath, and Outlook are becoming successful again because of saemankelyk, ‘Glory of the Dying God’ that is in Bastion
The man leads them to an inn, works to provide a cook and staffing at midnight per Clip’s request
Clip wants to go see the Dying God, even if the task detracts from their goal
Seerdomin walks his daily pilgrimage west of Black Coral to the Great Barrow of the Redeemer
Along the way are barrows for all of the casualties in the war against the Pannion Domin. Sometimes he thinks he hears voices of the dead
Seerdomin wears his old uniform in a way of self-flagellation, to openly bear hours guilt leaving himself vulnerable and draw the hatred of those around him

The Great Barrow had offerings of copper coins, sea-polished stones, fragments of glazed ceramics, feathers, knotted leather strips with dangling fetishes and rattling gourds, and clean skulls offered by a sub cult centered on the T’lan Imass
Seerdomin offers his himself as a gift of companionship to appease the Redeemer’s loneliness and humanity, as opposed to the worshippers elevating the Redeemer to a god
A woman calls Seerdomin ‘Benighted’

The woman is very young, wears a russet brown wool robe with green threads, a cropped pale green linen blouse. Has glistening black hair chopped short and angled down to her shoulders. Eyes dark brown
The worshippers of the Redeemer have claimed Seerdomin as the Redeemer’s chosen to guard his children, scares away thieves and rapists from hurting the pilgrims
The young woman believes the Redeemer teaches to embrace burdens on our souls
Seerdomin harshly rejects the duty imposed on him and leaves
Endest dreams back to when he was young, a third level acolyte in the Temple of Mother Dark in Kharkanas’ Citadel
Corpses along the moat leaked blood into the causeway
In the skies north of Kharkanas, waves of rainbow light slashed and devoured darkness
A wind and multihued light storm flared with thunderous fire above
Endest walked over and around bodies, sliding on pools of gore, to the Outer Gates of the temple
Inside the temple, the High Priestess and other priestesses writhed on the marble floors, crying out as if being raped, the tiles being covered in the women’s ‘nectar of ecstasy’ bodily fluids
The male priests and acolytes tried to help, but once they realized what the fluids were, they fled in fear and envy
Civil war in Kharkanas began
Endest watches as Anomander Rake approaches from the streets
Tiam’s blood flowed through Rake. His eyes glowed, black glistening scales covered his bare chest
Endest falls to his knees crying shot the end of the world, Rake tells him to follow him and face Mother Dark, for her to answer for the crime she committed this day
Endest wakes up in his room
Endest continues reliving the flashback, following Rake into the temple filled with corpses and blood
Rake tells Endest to hold until the day Endest needs to betray him
Endest then recalls Rake asking if Itkovian is incubating as a new god inside the Great Barrow
Endest does not know, Rake calls on Spinnock Durav but only at his own convenience
Continuing from the flashback in scene 4, Endest and Rake are running through the Kharkanas Citadel
Pass through corpses of Andii factions belonging to various people: Rake, Andarist, Silchas Ruin, Drethdenan, Hish Tulla, Vanut Degalla
As Rake approached the doors to the Temple, Mother Dark herself speaks to them
From Andii blood is born a new world. They are no longer alone, no longer free to play their vicious games. She senses Tiam’s blood in Rake
Rake embraced change, knows there will be wars between the Andii and that he will reunite them. Silchas, Hish Tulla, and Manalle flee
Mother Dark forsakes Rake and all her children because Rake killed Tiam and all of them took her blood
Endest falls to his knees and feels hope has been taken from his heart
Endest continues to look at the oil lamp flame
Wonders how loyalty can replace despair, if by placing despair on a leader, it can absolve them of the pain they inflict on others
After sleeping with the High Priestess, Spinnock sits naked on his bed oiling his sword, then gets up to sheathe it and hang it on the door
Spinnock has a copper-hued iron sword. The single heirloom of House Durav, made in a Hust Forge in Kharkanas, has had three previous owners
The High Priestess lying on the bed naked says he looks better naked
Spinnock says “You’re back.”

[Note: I’m not completely certain what happens here. My interpretation is that while she was asleep after sex, she “walks in Darkness and travels far”. This could either be literal and sex is apart of her ritual to open Kurald Galain, or this is a metaphor for getting tired with age and isn’t as energetic as her younger self was, which she reminisces in this scene]
Spinnock asks if Mother Dark has forgiven them, the High Priestess is shocked he can ask that question rather than mull over it for half the night, as depressed Tiste Andii can be
She responds the visions are more fraught

The High Priestess repeatedly expresses her gratitude for the good sex, is tired of the boring sex with the depressed Tiste Andii Priests, has him fetch her robes, and pleas for him to stay naked until she leaves
Spinnock cuddles with his sword as if making sure it knows it’s his one true love, all other women are distractions

Spinnock leaves and heads to the Scour Tavern, thinking about the kef tanar game he’ll play with Seerdomin and how he’ll continue to beat around this bush about the Great Barrow and his crisis of faith
Spinnock decides to take a detour and visit a priestess of the Redeemer in her home, her door marked with an imprint of the Great Barrow’s profile with an open hand below it
Spinnock met the priestess once while she was collecting wood at the ruin, and he wasn’t doing much at all
The priestess is old, obese, and eyes clouded with cataracts, sitting on a plush chair in front of a heap of trinkets, lit by two braziers
The priestess knows Spinnock Durav before he could introduce himself; only two Tiste Andii interact with humans. The other old man, Endest Silann, bargains for goods at the market
The priestess asserts the Great Barrow is outside the realm of Night, that the Redeemer does not kneel before Rake
Spinnock assures he that he is only concerned about Seerdomin as his friend
The priestess says Spinnock can’t help Seerdomin, and Seerdomin can’t help the followers of the Redeemer. Spinnock should talk to Seerdomin himself
‘The Redeemer is not afraid of the Dark’
Instinctively, Spinnock warns that the Redeemer should not embrace the Tiste Andii. It would destroy them both. ‘Fervent fever of gushing generosity’ is common to new believers of the Redeemer
Spinnock offers Rake’s help to the pilgrims for their any need, then offers his own personal aid. The priestess rejects both offers fearing they would infringe on the Redeemer’s domain
Kallor walks from the coast across the northern Lamatath prairies as ravens and vultures fly above him
Appears gaunt, with long unkempt gray hair, matted beard, icy blue eyes, wearing his long chain coat
Kallor asserts his heart is at peace, after a lifetime of being a supreme mad empire of a dozen terrible empires which he had to massacre thousands of his own subjects

Kallor feels being an emperor is an existence devoid of humor, all excesses and indulgences loses value, no profound revelation or answers to the great questions of life found looking at those that suffer, tortured or dying
The true enemy is banality
Kallor spooks a rabbit, kills it with a throwing knife, pulls outs its guts, and carries it for dinner
(Distant Past)
Kallor’s last empire existed 119,736 years before Burn’s Sleep or 3 years after the Fall of the Crippled God. It was built on K’Chain Che’Malle ruins and enslaved 12,000,000 people
Mages that wanted to defeat Kallor has trapped and brought down the Crippled God to rain down on the Jacuruku continent
The Elder Gods K’rul, Draconus, and Sister of Cold nights came together to curse Kallor with unending mortal life, never able to ascend to godhood
Kallor cursed them back: K’rul to be forgotten by the world ✅
, Draconus’ creation will turn on him✅
, Sister of Cold Nights (aka Nightchill) will walk among mortals and be torn apart on the battlefield ✅
K’rul swept the destroyed Kallorian Empire into the Imperial Warren
(Memories of Ice)
Kallor is Caladan Brood’s second-in-command. His tactics and mastery of campaigns is valuable to Caladan, but has no love from soldiers
Kallor hates Silverfox, because she contains Nightchill’s soul, one of the three that cursed him. Truly thought she was a threat and wanted her dead

Gethol (Gothos’ brother) visits Kallor to offer him the position of High King. In exchange for revealing Moon’s Spawn’s location, the Crippled God will give Kallor a moment of vulnerability against Silverfox
The Crippled God’s poison allows his servants to freely travel through the warrens
Kallor’s knowledge on K’Chain Che’Malle civilization gives them info on the undead K’Chain Che’Malle they’re fighting against
A group of KCCM Matrons resurrected the primitive K’Chain Nah’ruk (Short Tails) for unknown reasons which led to civil war and the downfall of KCCM
Kallor is the one to propose the alliance split their armies between Setta and Lest, then converge on Maurik, suspicious of the Malazans because they just discovered their outlawry was a ruse
Outside Coral, Kallor took his chance to attack Silverfox. He injures Korlat, pierces Whiskeyjacks chest killing him, then calls out to the Crippled God for help and he escapes into a miasmic warren
Kruppe muses on the various slices of civilian life in Darujhistan
Torvald Nom sneaks into an estate to rob them
The guards Milok and Doruth end up fighting because one confesses that he’s been sleeping with his wife who has a high sex drive and desire for variety
The house cat is affectionate with Torvald Nom, but doesn’t give him away
Inside, Torvald enters a study and finds scrolls including
A treatise of drainage grooves in stone gutters in the Gadrobi district
Tales of Pamby Doughty and the world inside the trunk
Lost verses of Anomandaris by the vellum makers guild of Pale, turns out to be empty
Illustrated guide to the headgear of cobblers in Darujhistan

Torvald breaks into the master bedroom, the estate owner’s wife is in bed and thinks Torvald is her husband that drank some male enhancement elixir and roleplaying as a thief, foreplay for procreating sex
While pretending to be the husband and raping her, Torvald successfully has her tell him that the treasure is under the bed
Torvald leaves with the excuse to drink more elixir, his heist is a success
Harllo is five years old, almost six. He lives with his adoptive family and assigns them numbers
Uncle One = Bedek, retired from being a caravan guard
Uncle Two = Gruntle
Uncle Three, Harllo, deceased and the boy’s namesake
Aunt One = Myrla
Aunt Two = Stonny Menackis
Harllo knows Stonny is his mother and is a child of rape, but doesn’t know what rape is
Cousin One = Snell, his abuser
Cousin Two = Mew, three year old
Cousin Three = Hinty, baby in a cradle
[Note: Here we get a vague timeline, at least six years past after the events of Memories of Ice.]
Harllo had come home with stolen vegetables, the adoptive parents are delighted by the sudden bounty of food and prepare the meal
Gruntle appears with wine and smoked horse meat, joining them to eat
Myrla was severely weakened after giving birth to Hinty, Harllo had the oldest sibling responsibility of taking care of the kids when Myrla couldn’t
Gruntle and Bedek talk about their past jobs as caravan guards
Myrla fed dung into the hearth pot fire, Harllo anticipates leaving in the morning to avoid Snell, to collect more dung along the West Shore of the lake
Duiker throws a years worth of writing into the fireplace, frustrated that he can’t clearly remember the Chain of Dogs
He remembers the names of Coltaine, Bult, Lull, Sormo Enath but not their faces

Duiker muses on how he’s unable to assimilate into his peaceful life, he feels like he has a mindless, pointless existence, how everyone feels isolated in their own world anonymous to each other, the illusion of free will
Mallet observes Duiker in thought and sympathizes that he feels useless
Believes retirement is accepting you are no longer worthy of value
Believes their hunter is not an issue. Antsy wants to dig up a dozen cussers. Blend is looking for the Assassin’s Guild HQ. Picker and Bluepearl are looking for the contractor.
Duiker retires to bed, has an invitation for lunch with Baruk the next day
Thordy is a gardener and vegetable merchant, whose produce was stolen twice this week by [Harllo]
Gaz, her husband, had lost all his fingers in a fishing accident. He just stormed off because she didn’t have enough money for him to drink. He’s an angry drunk but never physically accuses his wife
Thordy has become numb to Gaz’s verbal abuses
Nou, their watchdog, hates when Gaz is drunk but never attacks him. Dogs can sense bad intentions and doesn’t with Gaz
However, Thordy has been having thoughts of murdering Gaz while Gaz has expressed thought of depression and suicide
Gaz still loves his wife Thordy, even knowing she doesn’t love him back
Has killed four people to prove his worth and feel like he has some power, knowing he’ll pick a fight with someone that will kill home one day
Going to the alley behind Blue Ball Tavern, Gaz meets a god who states Gaz has made sacrifices to him 6 times now, consecrating any ground wherever he murdered
Simply draining life into the grounds is enough to summon the god. Gaz is to continue harvesting souls until the god is ready to give him further directions
Gaz’ wants are irrelevant
Gaz hears flies buzzing in his head, leaves to find someone to kill to get rid of it
Rallick Nom waits outside an old colleague’s tenement, Krute of Talient
Krute brings him up for a drink and updates him on the current situation
Talo Krafar’s son, Seba Krafar, won the succession crisis and has taken over the Assassin’s Guild
Lots of good assassins were disgusted with the leadership and left. Went to Elingarth, Black Coral, or Pale to join the Malazan Claw
There was a secret cult that admired Rallick’s philosophy of no magic. Seba Krafar tried to squash the cult, Krute has been ostracized even by old contacts
Rallick Nom says Vorcan also is back and makes it known he is not going to do anything to take over the Guild as the cult wants
Rallick Nom leaves and seems like he’s excited to do something
Iskaral Pust runs through the streets of Darujhistan, looking into every alley, while the bhokarala mimic his every move
Pust finds Darujhistan’s Temple of Shadow and knocks on the face of Baran, a charging Hounds of Shadow are sculpted into the door
High Priestess Sordiko Qualm, a tall woman with rust red hair, is obliged to welcome Iskaral Pust as a guest, though skeptical of his claim as High Priest and Magus of Shadow
The bhokarala enter the Temple despite there being wards, surprising the priestess

cards.h: Scene 9 (Daru Streets/Temple of Burn, Mappo Runt)

i.html: Mappo spooks an older town guard, feels relief he didn’t cause a heart attack to the very first person he meets
Mappo asks for directions to Burn’s Temple, the guard escorts him to avoid the drunken fete crowds from being spooked and cause a riot
En route, they encounter two corpses. The guard concludes the injuries match four previous corpses found
[Note: Gaz, the fingerless murderer]
The guard wonders why anyone would be so violent during times of peace, wishes to shake reason into them and understand why they hurt and murder

Mappo retorts that there is no reason. They are the result of savagery mated with little intelligence, fated to die afraid and alone understanding that all sense of power they once felt was all an illusion
They reach the Temple of Burn, desecrated with graffiti of prayers and curses. They pleasantly bid each other farewell
Before Mappo could knock, the Priest of Burn opens the door anticipating Mappo’s arrival and separation from Icarium
The priest and acolytes have been preparing a ritual for Mappo
Mappo plans to travel through Burn’s flesh to reunite with Icarium, knowing Burn’s flesh is poisoned
The Priest leads to a fissure where a temple dais would’ve been, below a flowing stream of molten rock. The Gate to Burn
The priest needs to bath Mappo in blood
Barathol walks with Scillara smd Chaur through Darujhistan
Barathol sees Scillara hurt, smiling at him when she notices he’s perceiving her
He thinks Crokus is a fool, Scillara is beautiful. Longing for something gone is pointless
Barathol thinks about leaving longing being is Seven Cities, too late was something that can’t be changed, too late in saving the people of Aren from the T’lan Imass
After leaving Aren, Barathol killed everyone in a raider camp, was saved by a caravan, gave them the raiders’ horses
The caravan let him keep the strongest horse, and gave him food, water, supplies, and directions to a Mezla waystation that could offer him aid
The caravan warned not to let longing trap him and drag him into the reaper who chases him
Scillara laughs that Barathol led them into a red light district
They get worried how Chaur feels around sexual stimulation and leaves
Scillara asks the toughest question, what to do with the rest of their lives
Barathol is content with honest work as a smithy
Scillara immediately plans a list of tasks, equipment, location, guild fees, etc. Barathol is glad for her help
Scillara suggests they wait around until a street food table opens up for them to take
(Picker)
Picker, Blend, and Antsy are eating at a spot a bard [Note: Fisher Kel Tarth] suggested they go for the rest of the week
While Blend is playing footsy with Picker, Picker watches [Barathol, Scillara, and Chaur] sit at a table
Picker thinks Barathol looks alot like Kalam, and that he might been a Claw hunting them down
Blend, who thinks [Scillara] is attractive, decides to walk over and all them directly
(Barathol)
Barathol recognizes right away that Blend is Malazan
Blend says she knows Kalam, Barathol admits they’re related like cousins
Blend affirms they’re retired and not looking for trouble, invites them to K’rul’s Bar which they own and winks at Scillara before walking away
Barathol thinks the Malazans are Bridgeburner deserters who knew his relative that was a Claw and Bridgeburner
Scillara heard the Bridgeburners are the nastiest company that started in Seven Cities and left with Dujek
Scillara looks at their direction, holds their eye contact, then buys them a pitcher to flirt as a power move
Picker’s group receives Scillara’s wine bottle
Picker sends Scillara white apricot nectar
Antsy is paranoid the wine is poisoned, after some they all drink the wine which turns out to be mid
Scillara walks over to say the drink she got is terrible and declares war
Scillara orders the Malazans a multihued insect shaped bottle
The waiter thinks both tables are in some freaky deaky shit (two men and one woman at one table, one man two women at the other) and storms off to talk to his manager
Antsy volunteers to drink first
It’s Quorl Milk, sold exclusively to women trying to get pregnant. A dose is a thimble, Green Moranth brand is the cheap brand
Picker waves a handkerchief in surrender, anticipates offering Scillara a week’s stay as the reward for winning
Antsy takes a shot and passes out, Picker makes sure Blend hires a carriage to take them home before they take shots and pass out
Crone watches Baruk summon an apparition with jade eyes
Baruk had captured the soul of a human from the Crippled God’s realm. The soul was meditating, separated from his body, in search of the Crippled God
Baruk previously had Shadowthrone as a guest, wants Crone to warn Rake about working with Shadowthrone
Baruk is wary of all the gods eager for a war as long as something else does the fighting for them
Crone retorts that Rake is blind to nothing, that he will deal with it directly
In turn, Crone warns that a threat is coming in the night that will pluck Baruk’s wards to announce her arrival and desperation
From spending time with Baruk, Crone has received confirmation that Shadowthrone speaks true, which would ease Rake’s mind
Crokus stands outside the Phoenix Inn, scared things can never be the same again, can’t go back to the way things were
Crokus hears a boot scrape two steps behind him, spins around while drawing his daggers, and thrusts with his right dagger
Rallick steps back and moves to parry with a tjaluk pig sticker knife
Crokus twists his right dagger to cut the palm Rallick’s parry hand, then slashes with his left dagger towards Rallick’s right knee cap
Rallick evades the left dagger
Crokus darts to Rallick’s left, attacks Rallick’s thigh then hip
Rallick parries all of Crokus’ attacks and draws a second tjaluk
Crokus throws his right dagger
Crokus realizes the enemy is dual wielding knives and calls out Rallick’s name

Mocks the High Priestess trying to find an answer through sex

Let Darkness receive my every breath
With her own

Anomander Rake, the Son of Darkness, had led the Tiste Andii out of Kurald Galain. The Tiste Andii felt betrayed when Mother Dark helped in birthing Light. Mother Dark turned away from her children and the Tiste Andii have been depressed ever since.

Rake attempted to lead the Tiste Andii into causes greater than their own, defending free people from the conquest of the Malazan Empire, hoping it would return the zest of life to his people. Their home, Moon’s Spawn, was parked over Pale to hold the Malazans off in the Siege of Pale for two years. The siege killed a great number of Malazan soldiers and reduced the Bridgeburners from 1400 to ~39.

In Darujhistan, Rake makes an alliance with the T’orrud Cabal through Baruk as the last standing free city on Genabackis. He is responsible for starting the internal war of the Assassin’s Guild to delay the Malazans from putting a contract to kill the cabal members. Rake joins Paran’s battle against the Hounds of Shadow because he does not want Shadowthrone to interfere with his battle against the Malazan Empire, leading to Cotillion’s release of Sorry/Apsalar.

For the hell of it, Anomander Rake attends Lady Simtal’s Gedderone’s Eve Fete and partners with Rallick Nom as his “second” in his duel against Turban Orr (though Rallick kills Turban Orr without help).
Anomander Rake feels he doesn’t need to fight the Jaghut Tyrant, other forces (like the Azath) can deal with it. Instead he fights the Lord of Galayn demon that Adjunct Lorn summons
(Memories of Ice)

Salind is one of the first born of the Tenescowri

The Hounds of Shadow left him this morning
