The shepherd plans to fling a copper coin with the face of the last tyrant of Darujhistan into the land at dusk
Harllo may never see the sun again
Traveller and Samar Dev are traveling together, two days away from reaching Karsa who chases the Skathandi raiders
Traveller notes the Lamatath Plains reminds him of his home in the Dal Honese savannahs
There were few herds of animals (bhederin, antelope, hares, wolves, coyotes, bears), wonders of the conflagration of Morn or K’Chain Che’Malle wiped out life in the region

The Kindaru were enthusiastic about having a new legend to tell, Traveller the Master of Wolf-Horses (the Hounds of Shadow that they briefly saw escort him) and the woman who rides the sacred Jhag brother to their horses-of-the-rock whom they cherished
Traveller had a feeling Samar Dev had more emotions tied to Karsa to have traveled through warrens and plains just to deliver his horse
Samar Dev simply days he dislikes slavers which is why he chases the Skathandi
[Note: Karsa’s adventure to Lether started because he briefly heard there were slavers in Sepik]
Samar Dev warns Traveller about the danger ahead and explains her story with Karsa and Emperor Rhulad
Believes Karsa killed the emperor cursed with reincarnation by the Crippled God’s sword, like to believe Rhulad thanked Karsa for ending his torment
Samar has not seen Karsa since he fight Rhulad
Samar believes Karsa pretends to be a dumb savage, but will do the opposite of the obvious result
The Traveller wonders if Karsa replaced Rhulad and if he wields the cursed sword. He isn’t and doesn't want to be an enemy of the Crippled God, but will face Karsa to destroy the cursed sword
The Traveller once played the game of civilization but in the end is a savage
Samar says all fools, civilized or barbarian, are the same
The Captain doesn’t remember anything before he was crucified. He guessed he was 11 years old at the time
Hands nailed to cross, feet crushed by hammers and buried in the ground
Ants crawled up and nested in his skull, tastes acid on his black tongue
Pulled his hands from the cross and crawled half a league (1.5 miles) to a dried riverbed where spirits rose to inhabit his body
His “kingdom” has been in perpetual motion, nonstop movement for 7 years
The main palace is pulled by 500 slaves. Rotates with another 500 slaves among the entourage wagons where they labored for the cooks, weavers, and carpenters until their turn to pull the palace
200 knights total among two wings of cavalry
Behind the palace, a mobile kraal of 300 well bred horses valuable to horse traders
300 horse warriors that range in raiding parties of 30
Dispatched emissaries to Darujhistan, Kurl, Saltoan, New Callows, Bastion, and Sarn. Waiting for Elingarth’s civil war to end before reaching out to them
A messenger comes and reports a second raiding party near the Kindaru were slaughtered
Troop Leader Uludan thinks the location was coincidental, not done by the Kindaru
Karsa Orlong appears. The palace halts for the first time in 7 years
Karsa destroys the wooden spar, freeing the chains of the slaves, and claims they are free
The spirits flee from the Captains body, the ants swarm in his head
The Captain sends the messenger to invite Karsa to be his dinner guest, wants him to be his heir, believes that Karsa will kill him before the day is over
Nimander’s kin stopped south of Sarn to give the horses time to rest up
The Dying God priests left crates full of ripe fruits, rock candy dusted with salt, bread, dried eel, wine, and cheese
Kedeviss leans against the wagon wheel, watches Kallor
Kedeviss is known to look at someone as if staring into their soul and knowing everything about them
The look made people fear her or fall in love with her, for Nimander it’s both
Nenada wants to banish Kallor by throwing rocks and dung at him
Desra thinks Nimander is the only one Aranatha would listen to look at Clip’s catatonic body
Nimander doesn’t understand why, Aranatha is not a healer
Aranatha is sitting fawn like, legs tucked underneath her, picking white flowers. She asks if he can feel her
She smiles, gives him the flowers, and walks over to Clip, Nimander is struck with an attraction to her
Kallor tries to touch Aranatha’s butt, she shoves him off of the wagon
Kallor laughs but looks unnerved that he was pushed
She asks Nimander a second time if he can feel her
Endest reminisces about his youth as a student and Dorssan Ryl, the river that wrapped around Kharkanas
There was an artistic movement of the 93rd century called the Flowering Bright where Mad Poets had a style characterized by brevity
Water in Darkness, dreams in sleep
Essence of truth, senses will lie
Certainty scours, a world without wonder
Endest ponders if the idea of water enough of an illusion to fool the senses
Before Light existed, there was nothing to reflect on water, only sensation when putting your fingers in it
Beside Dorssan Ryl, Endest had seen a woman he loved go mad, most Tiste Andii had when Mother Dark turned away from them
Endest imagined drowning her to see her eyes have expression again, but it did not happen. He watched her walk away, Kharkanas’s population all left to search for Mother Dark
Endest runs into Anomander Rake in a corridor where a human servant hung up tapestries of Kharkanas at random
Rake was looking upon a tapestry with a white skinned and onyx eyed figure wielding swords stands atop bodies bleeding from wounds on their backs
Locqui wyvals with female heads fly above the figure
Rake says “he” did not mean it, he was used badly. Endest remarks Rake forgives too easily
Endest heard that the river flowing into Coral Bay reminds people of Dorssan Ryl, wants to make a trip to see if its true
Rake doubts it, but gives permission if he comes back before the month passes
The next day, Endest leaves
Sitting at a fireplace, Rake asks Spinnock to go on a journey for him, but first asks about his game and Seerdomin
Spinnock is surprised Rake knows about Seerdomin
Spinnock is concerned that Seerdomin is distracted and losing all of their games together
Rake admired Itkovian as an extraordinary man who probably wouldn’t like his cult
Itkovian felt like he failed Capustan, though Rake thinks even the Crimson Guard wouldn’t have been able to defend the city. Itkovian was a man who could forgive everyone but himself
Spinnock remembers he was ordered to chase a dragon during the Siege of Capustan
Rake ponders why the Redeemer assumes his worshipers crimes, but not demand something in exchange
They are absolved, but not redeemed
Spinnock thinks about a woman, Rake is looking down at his boots frowning
Spinnock says Seerdomin has a crisis of faith, he stopped making his daily visit to the Great Barrow and failing to meet the expectations of his unwanted followers
Rake also notices Spinnock is speaking more carefully, abnormal for him
The Redeemer can’t deny the needs of his followers and is in a state of imbalance
Seerdomin is the one absolutely refusing them
Rake asks if sending Crone’s grandchildren to look over Endest’s journey would be offensive to him
Spinnock says it might be so it anyway
Rake agrees and gives good regards to the High Priestess
Spinnock thinks about visiting High Priestess
The priestesses are connected to Kurald Galain through sex.. for some reason
After sex with the High Priestess
The emanation/voice from Kurald Galain had stirred the Dark priestesses and made them frantic to take Andii and even humans to bed
Thinks about how Korlat had Whiskeyjack, how short humans lived, if Korlat would had to live through Whiskeyjack’s aging
The High Priestess feels something about Spinnock is different
Spinnock gives her Rake’s regards, surprising her
The High Priestess thinks both Rake and the Temple have failed
The Tiste Andii did not have purpose being involved in the struggles of lesser people. The Temple of Dark failed to rebirth the Gate and have Mother Dark return
Spinnock realized he interpreted Rake’s words wrong, perhaps he meant send his regards to the Redeemer’s priestess, Salind
He asks about her thoughts on the Redeemer cult
The Redeemer would be destroyed if he embraced the Tiste Andii
The cult is not organized and doesn’t have a doctrine. It is young and will be defined by what happens now
Spinnock realizes he forgot to oil his sword, the High Priestess remarks he back to his normal self again
(Salind)
Salind hides in her makeshift shed, turning away everyone
She feels crushed by the responsibility of being the Redeemer’s High Priest, failed to bring back Seerdomin as the Benighted
Gradithan continues to terrorize and rape the pilgrims, many plan to leave when the rain stops and the roads dry up
Spinnock enters after assessing the state of the pilgrim camp
Salind has a fever, reflecting the Redeemer’s own sickness

Salind explains she is a Child of the Dead Seed, she didn’t have a name until she gave herself one months ago. She’s the only women that hasn’t been raped because her family succumbed to flesh-eating diseases
Spinnock plans to take Salind away and send healers to the rest of the camp. Wants to rebuild the camp
Salind demands not to be raped
(Spinnock Durav)
Spinnock carries Salind’s unconscious body in his arms outside, a crowd of bystanders surround them
Spinnock says Rake will be told of their troubles, the crowd leaves without a word
Spinnock thinks Rake must already know what’s going on, unsure if he leaves the responsibility to Spinnock or someone else. Thinks Salind is an answer to an unknown question or problem
Spinnock remembers a line of a Mad Poet
The moon does not rain, but it weeps
(Gradithan)
Gradithan, former Urdomen (elite heavy infantry of the Pannion Domin), was close to trying to kill Spinnock
Monkrat, short bald and bandy-legged priest in wool robes, is happy that the Redeemer’s priest is gone. They can do whatever they want
No chance of Seerdomin awakening to his holy role
Gradithan sends a lieutenant to follow Spinnock, then inform their network in Black Coral that everything is taken care of at the Great Barrow, then return before dawn
Gradithsn looks at Silanah’s tower, planning it will be destroyed
(Silanah)
Silanah sees and knows Gradithan’s plan
Quotes a Mad Poet, ‘Mercy in compassion, no dragon lives’
Nimander goes through more streams of consciousness
Thinks about rage, how moderate skill with swordfighting needed rage. Rage that breaks pottery. Pots of kelyk clanking the sides of the wagon, holding its own kind of rage
Recalls while he was with Adjunct Tavore’s fleet, he would drink with the Malazans and listen to Deadsmell musing if battle rage being a gift from the gods
Getting drunk off the rum made Nimander think of his home living with Rake and the rest of his siblings

Endest Silann was nanny to Rake’s children, keeping them fed, clothed, and healthy. He kept from getting too close knowing the sad future that awaited them. He was like an ogre but never hurt or chased them
Rake’s children knew this and would mock Endest and play pranks on him, like rolling a breaker in his way so he would trip and fall
Andarist suddenly came, Rake’s older brother, and they would argue being closed doors for days before coming to a decision
Andarist would open a portal and take them all to Drift Avalii
Endest wept watching them go
Andarist was a tough teacher training them as soldiers, they came to love
Children were perfect soldiers, no fear of death, yet to develop their sense of empathy
Children knew rage, and the vessel breaks
Tying everything together, the Dying God is a child whose vessel leaked, and the priests would pour into the vessel and drank what came though
Nimander recalls another memory, two naked Dal Honese people that tried to paddle in an old bout to Geni island but instead nudged to Drift Avalii
Came from dark jungles, customary to bury their dead in mud walls that make up their huts, three dead make up a room roofed with palm fronds. Some houses were mazes in castles
Feeling like their ancestors judging them eternally drove some people insane
The jungle soil was not suitable for farming, the trees were impervious to fire and axes. Wars started over land, villages burned, people fled
The two Dal Honese people build a new boat and paddled away from Drift Avalii
Kallor remarks on the staked corpses, the crows wouldn’t look twice at the plants, says they [unclear if crows or plants] aren’t native to this world. Nothing changes
Skintick accuses Kallor of perpetuating the lie that nothing changes to make younger generations live in ignorance while the older generation continues to live in comfort
Nimander asserts that they’re going to find the Dying God to get Clip’s soul back
Kallor wishes them good luck but won’t help anyone. Especially Rake’s children
Kallor asks what they’ll do when they meet their father, Rake. He is great at starting things, but has trouble finishing them
Admits to fighting wars and allying with Anomander Rake, Caladan Brood, and Prince K’azz D’avore (the last whom he never met)
Kallor does not want to go to Black Coral, willing to wait centuries for Rake to no longer being angry with him [after killing Whiskeyjack]
Skintick sees [Azath] ruins fifty steps away from the Dying God farms
One story high, large stones with no mortars, dead trees that grew on top with roots that shaped to the floor. A pot with two dead flowers is the “garden”
Kallor recognizes the ruins as Jaghut and walks over, pushing a staked corpse out of the way
Skintick hopes Kallor finds his own selfish reason to deal the Dying God. From the way Kallor spoke, he felt that Kallor was not a subordinate but an equal to Rake
Kallor knocks on the door, the Jaghut [Gothos] inside recognizes Kallor
The Jaghut didn’t care for news about the outside world because nothing changes, Kallor smirks at Skintick
The Jaghut invites them in anyways and makes tea, he ate the last batch of cookies
The room has two walls, the other two walls were missing and instead had glimmering ice barriers
The Jaghut ignores Kallor asking his name, instead talks about beast gods and a wolf god that visited
Recognizes Skintick and Nimander are Rake’s children. Basically says he can scratch their skin and his DNA (every truth of you) collects in his fingernail
Every generation is different, eventually new breeds evolve. Is the progenitor or the first ancestor a god?
Kallor is impatient with such philosophy, says he’s killed a few Jaghut
The Jaghut continues. There was a gathering and alliance with the T’lan Imass to imprison his son Raest.
After, the T’lan Imass resumed their genocide. Kron of the Bek’athana Ilk clan and 43 hunters with a bonecaster found the Jaghut. That’s when the wolf god found him
The Jaghut killed all the T’lan Imass that found him, mocked the way Kallor had spoken
The Jaghut demands Kallor try the tea, then grips his wrist as he reaches for the cup
Kallor struggles and can’t pull away
The Jaghut says Kallor hurt the wolf god when he destroyed his own realm
The Jaghut lets go, Kallor threatened to kill him, the Jaghut threatened to awaken the Azath
Kallor recognizes he’s Gothos and is scared
The tea makes Nimander and Skintick start to lose consciousness
Skintick falls to his knees
Nimander stumbles through the walls of ice
Author of Gothos’ Folly, a multi-volumed suicide note. Father to Icarium. Guardian of the Deadhouse, the Azath House in Malaz City across the street from Coop’s Hanged Man’s Inn.

In the distant past, Gothos witnessed Scabandari Bloodeye betray Silchas Ruin after Kurald Emurlahn shattered and they had just defeated the K’Chain Che’Malle. Mael convinces Gothos to use Omtose Phellack to preserve the land. This incidentally freezes the Death Hold on the Lether continent, meaning ghosts were more likely to linger instead of pass on. After Kilmandaros crushes Scabandari, Gothos capture’s Scabandari’s soul in a Finnest, a flint dagger that eventually ends up in the possession of an Imass, Ulshun Pral, son to Onrack the Broken and Kilava Onass.

When Fiddler, Crokus, Apsalar, and Rellock fast travel from Tremorlor to Deadhouse, they meet Gothos. Gothos was disappointed that they failed to imprison his son Icarium within Tremorlor. Icarium has dementia because he tried and failed to free Gothos from the Azath House (in the Jhag Odhan) when in reality he enjoys the solitude.
Gothos also has a brother, Gethol, who was formerly the Herald of High House Death. In Memories of Ice, Gethol presented Hood’s offer to

save the Grey Swords from the Tenescowri but was rejected after insulting Fener for his impending fall. Falling out of favor with Hood, the Crippled God recruited Gethol as Herald of his yet to be High House Chains. Gethol later recruited Kallor as King of High House Chains. In
Bonehunters, Gethol offered to restore Tene Baralta’s scars (because Tene was a vain person) for a favor with Empress Laseen, which never
came to fruition because Lostara Yil killed Tene Baralta.
Desra thinks about Andarist’s last words to her, ‘You must take the world as it is’
Thinks about how most people are weak, don’t see the world being the horizon, don’t want to think, ignorant
Most strong people were bullies that kept people thinking they are weak to control them, acting as their protectors until they disobey
Desra acknowledges she’s a bully, and wants to bully Clip when his soul returns
She’s found someone to be dependent on, but it’s not Nimander
Kallor returns to the reason, tells Aranatha to toss Clip away, and tells the kin that the Jaghut decided to use Skintick and Nimander
Desra runs towards the Azath house
(Skintick)
Skintick wakes up on a limestone platform 12 steps across, column stumps painted wine red encircle the platform
Ancient olive trees with twisted trunks, leathery leaves, and abundant clusters of fruit surround the platform
Corpses wearing brightly colored clothes, strange shoes, and gold on their teeth. All beneath the trees
Skintick felt the sun was evil and responsible for killing this distant world
Mini-2nd person POV
To dream of a future where your children could live, even if it’s being your control
In this dead world, someone seeded it and watched it grow, they made the sun angry, a momentary cough, to kill the planet
Skintick’s brain feels pain, believes the Dying God is dying because the world isn’t fair, everyone dies, everything is meaningless
Gothos slaps Skintick awake
Skintick laughs to protect himself from insanity, and calls him a bad choice for “this”
Gothos explains that at the moment of dying, people will feel like they’re not enough
Rake knew this, that living in one world was madness, so he “tore his people from complacency” and was cursed
The distant world was on the path of the Azath, Skintick felt free, which reaffirms to Gothos that he is a bad choice
(Desra)
Desra walks in, sees Gothos and Skintick slowly sitting up, but didn’t see Nimander
She follows Gothos’ gaze to the ice wall
As Nimander entered the realm, spirits pull at his body claiming him
The being called Elder grabs Nimander runs up a slope into a caldera where the spirits can’t reach
Elder has a child-like face, bald head, thick white long eyebrows. Round cheeks, thick lips, a pug nose, bulging neck wattle, bright yellow skin, emerald green eyes, dagger like teeth
The spirits are trapped in dragon blood
Elder builds Azath Houses, Gothos would come when he finds them “adequate” (which pisses Elder off because he works hard), walks inside, and places the last stone to leave
Nimander plans to have Elder do what Gothos does, stand inside the house as Nimander places the last stone for him to escape
Nimander is not heartless and can’t leave Elder behind in eternity
The gate is Omtose Phellack, but the realm is something else that Gothos doesn’t want to deal with
Desra yells at Skintick, Gothos says don’t blame anyone. Accidents happen
Rake chose wisely each time, Rake is the one person who earned his respect
Gothos also warns not to trust Kallor
Desra looks into the ice wall and sees movement
Kedeviss watches Kallor be nervous under Aranatha’s gaze
Kallor says Jaghuts can’t be trusted, that they should go straight to Coral and have Rake face the Dying God to get Clip back. Vengeance is all there is
Kedeviss thinks Kallor is being hunted because someone wants vengeance against him, Aranatha says its always been so
Nimander watches, helps, and waits for weeks as Elder built a house four stories tall that would fit him
Elder is able to build the house in a way that both would be inside and they could escape the realm, Nimander wants to stay
Nimander says he’ll be lost again if he follows to where Elder belongs
The spirits of the realm are Tiste Andii, Edur, and Liosan that died in the first wars when the dragons came
Nimander wants to share in the peace they have together
Elder says a new war will start to claim Nimander, Nimander is sad but will stay anyways
Elder thanks Nimander, who suggests punching Gothos in the face if he sees him
Elder helps Nimander through the window
The final stone is pushed through the window, Nimander’s fingertips are crushed and bleeding
Nimander uses his shoulder to support the bloody obsidian chunk and pushes it into place
Nimander falls down the caldera slope, the spirits grabbed and clawed at him, he surrenders
Nimander is pulled back into Gothos’ Azath House, Desra holds her injured and in her lap
Gothos calls him a fool, he needed to save Elder for later, and now there’s an Azath House in the blood of dragons. Dragons don’t play games
Nimander, Skintick, and Desra leave
Kedeviss sees Nimander and kin returning, orders Aranatha to cook and Nenanda to make a fire
Aranatha declines, she leaves to speak with Gothos
Kallor calls Aranatha an uncanny bitch
(The Captain)
The Captain and Karsa sit on carpets, a kettle with wine boils on a brazier between them
The Captain wants to make Karsa his heir and holds no ill will to him
Karsa calls slavery an abomination done by people who hate. Rejects all gifts. Will destroy his kingdom and make sure everything he built is forgotten
The Captain’s last words as he bleeds out to death, ‘You could have lied’
(Karsa Orlong)
Karsa looks at the feast he ate, then told the servants to take whatever they want
Followers would follow even to their own deaths, both that happened under Karsa and the Captain
Without followers, civilization can’t exist
Karsa wants to make the Teblor his companions, not followers, as they destroy civilization wherever they found it
To stop the breeding of followers that tyrants could manipulate with duty, honor, patriotism, freedom. To stop forces of destruction
Karsa kicks over the brazier and sets the palace on fire
Karsa stands in front of the throne the slaves are freed, officers will divide the loot equally, cheaters will be killed
The survivors are to go home or find a home, Karsa promises that he will come as a destroyer of cities. Live well until then
Karsa becomes the god of the Broken Face for years to come
On a low hilltop, Traveller tells Samar Dev that he led the Malazan armies
Served death in all they did. Imposed peace, ended feuds and tribal rivalries. Kept trade roads safe from bandits. Coins flowed.
‘With a cold smile he waits. Where all roads converge, where every path ends. He waits.’
They see flames from the Skathandi carriage burning
‘Karsa Orlong burns, Traveller. Because that is what he does. It’s a pyre. And he does not grieve. The Skathandi are no more’
Traveller feels frightened when she talks about Karsa
(Gaz)
Gaz observes his wife Thordy place flat stones in the vegetable garden
Views good lack of words a virtue of manhood
Doesn’t know what it’s for, might have to do something about it soon
Plans to kill something to satisfy the flies in his head and to avoid beating his wife
(Thordy)
Thordy thinks to herself as she lays down the stones
Thinks about freedom, how a mind could stop under too much pressure, how pleasant the stone slabs are
Thinks about how Gaz sleep talks and poured out words
Tales of gods and promises, invitations and bloodlust, the pain of maimed hands and what pain those hands could give
(Blacksmith Guild Office, Barathol)
Barathol walks in on an over-important clerk who gives him the run around and catch-22 on joining the guild
Can’t provide credentials, need a sponsor, can’t apprentice because he’s overqualified and too old, can’t meet a blacksmith for privacy reasons
The Malazan Empire busted closed shops and charged for monopolizing industries, but Darujhistan was never conquered and thus not law here
(Darujhistan, Barathol)
Barathol goes outside to Mallet who’s eating purple ice in a leaf cone
Decides to open up an independent smithy anyways
His work meets the standard of the old Malazan Empire, the new embassy has guards, deserters from the northern Malazan campaigns
Can have a mutual agreement to funnel business between K’rul’s Bar and Barathol’s smithy
Barathol asks Mallet to accompany him to find a suitable location
His idea makes Mallet laugh

cards.h: Scene 5 (New Noblewoman’s Estate, Scorch and Leff)

i.html: Scorch and Leff try to apply as gate guards for a noblewoman moving into Darujhistan
A bowlegged Gadrobi foreman gives them a hard time then gets castellan Studlock
Studlock walks over

Wears many layers of cotton, a hood, a mask with a red unhuman glint behind the holes, gloves held up like a praying mantis, feet like hooves, a voice like gravel under nails, and has to take 3 steps for every 1 step of the bowlegged foreman
Studlock asks Leff Bahan to stick out his tongue and says he has greva with parasites from eating raw lake conches and Studlock will provide treatment
Barracks are being readied and need to hire three more guards
Studlock assesses they are dumb but loyal and hires Scorch and Leff
Orders Scorch to go find more guards while he heals Leff
The foreman smirks noted from the ominous narrator
(Torvald Nom)
Tiserra tells Torvald that she wants to do some things by herself like go to the market and not be together all the time
Torvald agrees to keep his wife happy and goes to the Phoenix Inn
Scorch approaches Torvald
(Leff)
Studlock brings Leff into an annex of the estate, digs through a crate with straw, and pulls out a glass bottle
Drop it into the eyes and tongue x3 times a day until there’s no more, should deal with the Greva worms
Studlock suggests Leff may have other worms like suspicion and guilt that treat symptoms like irrational fear of fish hooks
When asked if he’s a healer, he’s whatever you need him to be
Studlock goes to look for a uniform for Leff
(Torvald)
Torvald wonders how to tell Tiserra about how he got a new job
Wonders who the new noble is and why the castellan is wrapped up like a corpse
Studlock is delighted to have another hire and immediately assesses Torvald to be Captain of the Guards
Studlock asks if there will be conflict of interest between House Nom and the lady who’s expected to fill a seat on the city council
Torvald tries to explain that he’s not necessarily cast out, Studlock directly pins it to his lack of ambition
Leff appears, his lips and bulging eyes are bright orange
Reminds Scorch of a cat that Leff sat on
Torvald explains humans can’t get greva worms, only fish
Studlock shrugs and guesses Jurben worms, Torvald explains they live in green gas pockets underground and are as big as a person’s leg
The spectre of misdiagnosis haunts us all. I do aplogize, Leff. Perhaps your ailments are due to another malady. No matter, the drops will wash out in a month or two
Studlock plans to take them to get their uniforms in the house colors, black brocaded with gold thread, and explain their job roles
Torvald gets paid 20 silver councils a week, the guards gets paid 15 silver councils a week
[Note: For reference, Scorch and Leff’s last job was 2 councils per week. 300 councils keeps a family comfortable for years]
They all quickly nod in agreement
Murillio walks to Stonny’s dueling school and thinks about how he’s getting old, the incident wouldn’t have happened if he were younger
At the school he saw about 20 overweight kids practice badly at swordplay while Stonny’s more focused on fixing her gloves
Thinks Murillio is old money with his dirty clothes, says the waitlist is full for enrollment
Surprised he wants to teach

Murillio was a student of Carpala, someone who took students every three years, hates teaching and dueling because all of his students were either killed, abused alcohol, or in Murillio’s case chased women
Stonny thought there were 7 disciples left in the city, Murillio says 2 of them died
Fed broke his neck falling down stairs, Santbala was killed in a duel against Gorlas Vidikas
Murillio plans on teaching footwork, fleeing, defense, and non-lethal stop-hits to knees, wrists, and feet
Myrla appears, tells Stonny that Harllo has been missing for two days
Stonny thinks it’s Snell’s fault because he’s been stealing her money meant for the family
Murillio offers his network of connections to help find him. Asks for his description and behavior
Stonny runs off, Myrla explains to Murillio that it’s actually Stonny’s son
Snell is a psychopath
Wants his mother’s sole love and attention, but does not care if she cries because of him
Thinks he deserves everything as his birthright, injustice is anything taken from him
Snell goes to Two-Ox Gate to make sure Harllo is dead, gets distracted throwing rocks at lepers and plans to celebrate by killing one on the way home
Harllo is not there, Snell runs back thinking Harllo faked his death and wants to kill Harllo before he could reveal
Want revenge on Stonny for hitting him over the money he stole from her
Gorlas dines with Challice as he thinks about killing the famous duellist [Santbala] made him famous to be rich, but not disgustingly rich
Thinks money is the only god worth worship
Tells Challice that he’ll be taking a trip to visit mines he became the overseer of [Eldra Iron Mongers mine granted by Humble Measure] and to go to Gredfallen Annexe to finalize a contract
While he’s away, he expects Challice to host Shardan Lim and Hanut Orr. He wants to pimp her out, pay back favors and in the future take everything they own
Thinks Challice worships money too and would happily do it
An hour and a half after the dinner, Gorlas takes his carriage out of the city past Two-Ox Gate
Sees the lepers outside the city, when he is a ruler of Darujhistan he plans to kill them all and bury them in a mass burial pit
Challice looks at her half moon globe thinking about her future
Knows Shardan and Hanut won’t be the only ones to solicit sex, more men will come
Thinks one will fall in love with her, and she can use the opportunity to betray Gorlas
Challice looks at herself in the mirror, this she’ll be a different person after this, and gets ready to head out
Scillara approaches Duiker, relating that he survived the Chain of Dogs and she was in Sha’ik’s camp
By Fisher’s advice, she mentions she was with Heboric until he died
Duiker was hopeful for a second, gets sad that his friends die. Solars days it makes room for new ones
Scillara wants Duiker to accompany her to the Phoenix Inn
Duiker doesn’t want to, but agrees when she draws attention to her chest and wants to embarrass a friend [Crokus]
Crokus sits down to eat with Kruppe as Rallick is angry
Kruppe says Crokus followed in Rallick’s shadow, may have kept his name instead of changing it to Cutter if he followed Murillio
Crokus denies being in anyone’s shadow and is reminded of Shadowthrone
Kruppe talks about shadow, and Crokus wants to avoid them especially Apsalar who broke good heart
Kruppe keeps eating and wants to take Crokus to a cemetery to pick out with bones died healthy and which bones died happy
Kruppe thinks Murillio died now that he’s boring and wants Crokus to throw him off a cliff if he ends up like Murillio
Murillio enters
Mogora moves and shifts around to block Iskaral’s view of High Priestess of Shadow, Sordiko Qualm
Sordiko came to terms that he is the High Priest of Shadow and that’s why she hasn’t kicked them out
Sordiko hates that Mogora is a witch of Ardatha the Queen of Spiders, and hates that the bhokarala locked themselves in the cellar
Sordiko approaches and tells them she wishes they’d both commit suicide
Mogora wants to go shopping, threatens to have sex if he doesn’t go with her. Iskaral agrees
Gorlas’ mine region was a massive pit, facing a cliff with caves and tunnels
The town had 800 people with workers, slaves/prisoners, security, crafters, food, and health care staff
All trees a mile and a half around the camp were cut down
Gorlas talks to the foreman who does all the day to day necessity work
Kids would be bought from poor families to work the mines where adults can’t reach. Rule that one can touch the kids
A miner averages 50 years. If they can’t work anymore, they can be shift captains
The slaves can’t complain because the mines send them for the most dangerous jobs like working the more dangerous veins where many are killed by the arsenic and gold
The foreman plans on buying an estate and wife
Gorlas wants to finance the foreman’s estate because expected him to die in three years without naming an heir, thus giving Gorlas another property in the Estate District
Harllo is a mole, child laborer working in mines that only children can fit in
Bainisk is a 16 veteran mole. Half his face is scar tissue, has blue eyes
Harllo feels safe and protected in the tunnels, only broke a finger on his right hand so far
Harllo enjoys seeing things no else will. He also drags hoses for the workers to drain water. He’ll see strange growths on the stone and eats blind fish
Bainisk pulls Harllo from a fissure inside a cave, Harllo reports he saw iron 3 child hand lengths across
Bainisk says Harllo earned the afternoon rest, but Harllo doesn’t want to go back up top to the Chuffs camp because Venaz is bullying him
Earlier that morning, Harllo was littered into a crevasse so far below ground that the rock was warm, the air was hot and sulfurous enough to flare candles when lit
At the bottom, Harllo meets a T’lan Imass. Both legs shattered with bones sticking through leathery skin. He had a broken bag with two antler picks, a bone punch, and stone mallet
Dev’ad Anon Tol of the Irynthal Clan that lived on the shores of the Jhagra Til until Raest, the Jaghut Tyrant, enslaved them
Dev’ad’s clan were thrown into the crevasse, only he continued to live. Believes due to the Ritual of Tellann
Dev’ad was an inventor, his ideas made his clan, the bonecasters, and Raest afraid of him. He was thrown down here so that he and his ideas would die with him
Harllo tells him about what Gruntle taught him about T’lan Imass
Undead warriors at Black Coral kneeled to a man who died taking all their pain away. A barrow was built and Gruntle cried for him
Harllo offers to bring him up but Dev’ad declines
Harllo stays they have iron picks now.

Dev’ad calls iron ‘skystone’, Jaghut used sorcery to obtain iron and shake it. Imass were forbidden to witness the Jaghut process. Dev’ad thought about the potential of mining and shaping iron without magic
Harllo is being pulled up
To keep other people from finding Dev’ad, the Imass said to report of white rock that sickens people, foul air, and a ghost haunts this cave
Harllo is welcome to come back, Dev’ad requests splints but Harllo spent know what those are
Harllo wants to keep Dev’ad’s tools hidden or else Venaz would steal them
Scillara holds Duiker’s arm as they walk to the Phoenix Inn
Though struggling for conversation, Scillara carries it
Scillara thinks people in Genabackis look familiar to faces she would see in Seven Cities
History is pointless to Duiker because no one wants to listen
Scillara tells Duiker about Heboric, wanted to go to Otataral Island to return something he stole but was killed by T’lan Imass. The Imass also kidnapped Felisin Younger
[Note: Would Duiker recognize the name as the new Adjunct’s younger sister? Unsure at this point]
Scillara explains why she wants to go to the Phoenix Inn
Crokus had talked about Darujhistan nonstop during their travels, said he would show her everywhere. Scillara feels hurt and left behind
Now Scillara is with Malazans who find familiarity with Kalam’s relative Barathol, both are aware of his history as a Red Blade and his tragic involvement with the T’lan Imass massacre in Aren
They arrive at the Phoenix Inn
Duiker explains Kalam, Apsalar, and Kruppe have been here
Kruppe was an ambassador in the Pannion War who had confounded Caladan Brood, one of the greatest leaders in the continent. Crokus probably doesn’t know because he left for Seven Cities at this time
Murillio tells Kruppe about how Stonny’s son was possibly kidnapped
Kruppe teases Murillio might like Stonny,
Crokus offers to ask around the women on the docks floor more information
Scillara puts her hand on Crokus’ shoulder, Duiker pulls up two chair to their table
Murillio suddenly rises to formally bow to Duiker whom he met once before
Both Kruppe and Murillio are attracted to Scillara
Kruppe sends Sulty to buy the finest wine from another establishment, offending Meese. Costs 3 silver councils
Scillara quickly tells her story
Was a sex slave to Korbolo Dom’s traitor Malazan army
A Malazan priest [Heboric] took her and Crokus across half the continent

But by the Otararal Sea they were attacked. Heboric died, Crokus disemboweled, Scillara had a baby that she had no regrets leaving in [Barathol’s] village. The son of Osserc [L’oric] and villagers saved their lives
Crokus was tasked by the Rope to protect Felisin Younger, but nearly died and failed since she was taken
Crokus still is broken hearted despite all the sex they had together
Scillara says Crokus is embarrassed by her and that she’s too fat
Almost drowned when the moon shattered and fell from the sky, then rescued by a dragon [Lady Spite]
Everyone is stunned until Duiker smells the new great wine bottle and tells everyone to dump the trash from their cups
Everyone is happy to have Scillara spend the rest of the night elaborating on everything she said
Crokus tries to reassure that she’s not fat. Inside he thinks he’s too low for any woman
The table orders for another bottle and dinner as Scillara shares their story
Challice is dolled up in a green dress, dining with Hanut and Shardan
She’s attracted to both and ready to sleep with them
Hanut talks about how Gorlas saved Challice life the night his uncle [Turban Orr] and Shardan Lim’s uncle [Councilor Lim] were killed
Hanut wants Challice’s father to meet him and settle generations-long conflict between House Orr and House D’Arle
Challice says she has no power over her father’s opinion, especially being married into a lesser family
Hanut says Challice has been knocking back wine all night like a tavern harlot and storms off
Shardan Lim explains that Hanut wanted her father specifically to come to him, impressed that Challice stood up to the bully that he is, affirms they are not friends
Shardan apologizes that he failed to protect Challice, Hanut is probably spreading rumors that Gorlas is being cuckolded by Shardan to dishonor her
Shardan wants to know what Gorlas’ involvement in the iron industry is
Challice confronts Shardan about what he wants, should they have a love affair where she spills Gorlas secrets to Shardan whom she has no future with
Shardan is in love with Challice and wants her to have freedom and agency to make choices again
Shardan offers to duel and kill Hanut for Challice’s honor
Challice agrees to try this freedom of his, says she will not chain herself to another man, and feels his bowing to her makes this instance of infidelity feel noble
Night falls on Darujhistan
Challice has sex with Shardan, the second man she’s been with
Gaz stalks his next victim

Torvald ends his shift for the night, leaving Scorch and Leff to work. A two-person black carriage drops off a hooded figure who walks into the estate. Torvald chooses to ignore it to return home to his wife
A guard with occasional chest pain tries to find out more information on the the killer of a local man, but no one likes him
Humble Measure continues to plot the downfall of the Bridgeburners
Bainisk has lived all his life in Chuffs, enamored with Harllo talking about Darujhistan
Venaz used to be Bainisk’s favorite, jealous of Harllo who’s replaced him
Crone flies from Baruk’s tower

cards.h: Scene 1 (River outside Black Coral, Endest Silann)

i.html: Endest Silann hikes to the river with his walking stick
Disappointed it’s not Dorssan Ryl, the river in Kurald Galain
Endest wonders why he made the trip, perhaps to die on the return back
Endest walks over to a campfire her sees and is pleasantly surprised that its Caladan Brood
Caladan disbanded his army after the Pannion War, is a mystery like Anomander Rake. Instead of being shrouded in darkness, he’s covered in manners and politeness
Caladan expected a guest and prepared tea and cooked fish, also pleasantly surprised to find Endest
Caladan says other Tiste Andii have been lured to the river, he wishes he could tell them and ease their burden. Endest’s knowledge is incomplete
Something awaits the Tiste Andii
Endest doesn’t think forgiveness exists
[Note: Possibly Mother Dark forgiving the Tiste Andii for taking Tiam’s blood]
Caladan asks what about restitution, Endest cries and is amazed by the ambition to even think of that
Caladan is sure Endest will find his pilgrimage was worthwhile
Endest looks into the campfire and is reminded of Kharkanas burning, of Mother Dark turned away as her children died
Samar Dev and Traveller arrive at the burnt wreckage of the Skathandi carriage
Samar thinks about the irony of Karsa freeing slaves, yet when he cries Witness! he chains them to his narrative and history
Traveller is shocked that there’s no bodies, it’s as if Karsa walked up to them, said ‘It’s over’
Karsa’s lone trail heads north, they should catch up to him this day
Traveller is frightened even more, but still determined to see if he has the Crippled God’s cursed sword
Samar Dev and Traveller encounter three men and two pregnant women
Samar is impressed the men started to defend the women. Traveller asked Samar to check on the women as he spoke to the men on the side
Samar finds they are healthy, but annoyed their doe-eyes subservience is how she sees herself with Karsa
Traveller finds that Karsa wields a flint sword, was bequeathed the kingdom, and dispersed them taking nothing for himself
The people are Gandaru, kin to Kindaru and Sinbarl people
Not quite human, eyes like yellow grass, behavior like pretty animals. Dark skin, slopes brow, full lips, broad mouth
Once finished, they continue following Karsa’s trail
Samar observes that animals blend into their surroundings for camouflage as flowers grow bright to attract insects to help pollination. Nothing starts the same
Samar believes the Gandaru have to chance to survive against humans
Humans are unstoppable, if animals die out humans can replace them with livestock
Karsa is the only one that can destroy human civilization, and Samar Dev looked forward to it
Karsa stops, awaiting them
Samar yells at him, Karsa laughs and picks her up into a hug
Samar says down and she is dropped to the ground
Karsa assumes Traveller is her husband and wants to fight for her, Samar says she only belongs to herself
Karsa is wary of Traveller because he’s Malazan, Traveller recognizes the slave tattoos on his face
Karsa affirms he didn’t kill the Skathandi leader and killed Emperor Rhulad
Traveller doesn’t want to capture Karsa, sad that Karsa probably won’t tell him of his interesting life
Samar Dev wants to go home
Traveller suggests Darujhistan where she can take a ship
Karsa heard that Darujhistan won against and remains free from the Malazan Empire. Wants to visit then he’ll return home to the northern Genabackis to forge his army
Salind nearly dies from her fever, Tiste Andii priestesses call her soul back
Her soul sought a place of formless light with white sand
Naked pregnant women approach, hair covering their faces, the unborn souls appear as fist-sized suns with rainbow flames spinning above their mothers
As the mothers passed through Salind, she would see the souls’ complete life experience
A voice chanted to bless them in the name of the Redeemer and Daughter of Death to protect them from murderers
Salind races towards the droning voices inviting her to sanctuary
Salind wakes up in a bed surrounded by the priestesses, they immediately leave
Spinnock helps sit her up, he called a favor and the priestesses felt an obligation to save another priestess regardless of their patron
Salind realizes she is suicidal and wonders if hope is enough to keep living
Spinnock responds that blessing purchases a moment of peace, existing has value itself
Salind looks away to a wall with Andiian hieroglyphics and paintings of Mother Dark turning away from the Tiste Andii
Salind realizes the Redeemer brought her close to death to show what she needed to do and why she she was needed
Salind needs to return to the pilgrim camp, Seerdomin will appear when he is needed
Spinnock feels envy that her god spoke to her, something the Andii yearn but will never have from Mother Dark. He leaves her to rest
Salind beseeches Mother Dark to bless her children
Interprets the face candles burning bright that there was no darkness in the room as her answer
By lantern light, Seerdomin walks through the ruins of the old Coral palace previously occupied by the Pannion Seer
Seerdomin felt he and others committed crimes unjustifiable by coercion or being under duress
Recalls Malazans had died here, that Seguleh had slaughtered here
Four conspirators had meetings in the chamber where the K’Chain Che’Malle matron tortured Toc the Younger in its embrace
Seerdomin wields his tulwar, the first person who stood up had his face cut in half ☠
The looping backswing decapitates a second person to his right ☠
Seerdomin flips the table onto the third person, Hegest, to his left

The fourth person opposite Seerdomin tries to draw a dagger and reflexively covers his head, Seerdomin cuts through his arms and chops down the collarbone and the sternum, getting stuck in the ribs. Seerdomin has to kick the corpse away ☠
Hegest weeps, Seerdomin it was their mistake not expecting an “honorable” man like Seerdomin to commit such murder
Seerdomin interrogates Hegest, but makes no matter what Seerdomin is going to kill him
(Seerdomin)
Seerdomin kills Hegest after getting the information he wanted
A list of names and the plans to expel the Tiste Andii, plans that involved as far as the pilgrim camp
Suspected Salind of being part of the conspiracy
Seerdomin takes hidden tunnels to return outside and plans to go after the conspirators in the city
(Monkrat)
The rats spy on Seerdomin and report to Monkrat, a priest wizard that can manipulate spirits
Nimander’s kin arrive at Bastion, the city appears to be abandoned
The docks and lakebed are dry, the farmland has black dead plants and “scarecrows” not moving. Sigils painted black on the gate archway. Faint singing is heard
Aranatha says in a melodic voice that the entire city is the Abject Temple
Kallor once tried to sanctify an entire empire with him as a god, it failed as everything eventually does
A giant piece of machinery Kallor believes to be K’Chain Che’Malle appears to have crashed onto the street
Reminds Skintick of when Withal showed them old pumps under Dreth Street in Malaz City
The group breaks into an inn, the well in the courtyard is stuffed with bloated corpses
They leave the wagon and horses in the stable
Inside the well furnished foyer, tables and chairs were piled on one side, black ichor streaks everywhere
Bottles filled with kelyk behind the counters, ichor stained beds piled up at the base of the stairway leading up to the emptied rooms
The group starts donning their gear for battle. Weapons, chain hauberks, metal gauntlets
Nimander and Skintick scout first, Aranatha says they’ll know if they get in trouble
The main thoroughfare led to an round clearing with a giant alter surrounded by people wearing threadbare clothes, weapons held above their heads, black streaks in their mouth
The mob sings more ferociously as they walk towards Nimander and Skintick
Kallor appears and approaches with his greatsword, the crowd screams and runs to get out of his way
Kallor keeps walking to the altar unimpeded, the crowd surrounds him
Nimander feels pity for the people, wants to try to sneak Clip to the altar using their abilities as children of Night
Desra feels uncomfortable with hope
Aranatha has been so calm and senses Nimander and Skintick returning
Skintick found food and supplies as if they were just delivered, similar to the packages waiting for them asking the road to Bastion
Clip’s fever is getting worse
Crone flies directly over Silanah onto the balcony to meet Rake
Crone reports Baruk understands [something]
Something is happening to the south
Crone and her children have seen the people plan to make an attack against the Tiste Andii, “machinations of the surface crawlers” “the dark clouds breed a fierce storm”
Rake wants Endest to come back
Ten bells have sounded [Note: 10 in the morning?]’
Crone departs and wishes Silanah will also fly true when the time is night
Rake smiles and says there’s no need
The purest of artists are minds with childlike wonder and imagination
Child labor is akin to slaughtering artists
The adults that drive child labor are dead inside, walking corpses that resent everything beautiful in life
Harllo scavenged two emlava hind long-bones from the camp garbage heaps
Instead of going back to the camp after his shift ended, Harllo climbs down to give Dev’ad the bones as splints
As Harllo descends and rests on a ledge, he realizes he’s on the balcony of a buried building with windows
Harllo finds Dev’ad again
The Imass feels indebted because he can use the emlava bones to make legs for hotels
Dev’ad sees that Harllo’s nervous, tells him he should go back quickly to avoid punishment
Does not want Harllo to risk coming back, suggests he might be able to come to Harllo on the surface
Warns Harllo not to explore the buried buildings. It was a mystery to Raest, full of empty rooms and corridors that go nowhere
Night, Scorch and Leff are guarding the gates as Torvald went home
Madrun and Lazan Door arrive

Madrun is a large, broad shouldered man with short legs and shaggy hair like a yak. Wears a sky-blue blouse too small for him, hugs his arms tight and the sleeve cuffs at the middle of his forearms. A jester-like vest with bright green, orange, red, and yellow colors. A shimmering black kerchief is wrapped around his neck. Vermillion pants that end below the knees, calf high moccasin boots

Lazan Door is a tall skeletal thin bald man. Has a tattoo on his forehead in an oval frame with gold thread stitched into his skin. Has gold capped teeth with silver tips, looks like rows of fangs. Wears a threadbare linen cloak so long it drags behind him
Scorch goes inside and retrieves castellan Studlock
Stucklock has been reluctantly expecting Madrun and Lazan Door to come work as compound guards
Studlock is surprised they survived a mountain slide caused by [Burn’s Hammer] which made them late
Studlock leads them inside to meet Lady Verada
Torvald eats dinner as Tiserra stares angrily at him for breaking his promise that he wouldn’t work with Scorch and Leff again
Torvald leaves for work, to return by midnight
At the estate, Scorch and Leff tell Torvald about their new compound guards, acquaintances of the castellan whom they call Studlock
Torvald recognizes the full title as Studious Lock the Landless of One-Eye Cat
Blood Drinker, Bile Spitter, Poisoner
Torvald takes two steps into the estate and is greeted by Studlock who introduces Madrun Badrun and Lazan Door
Torvald is nervous and asks where their [Seguleh] masks are
Madrun asks Studlock for reassurance about their job
Torvald has not been to One Eye Cat, but heard the tales of Madrun and Lazan hired to oust the Malazan fist and things that happened after concerns him
Lazan says all the details after the Malazans were driven out are outrageous lies told by those who think they’re righteous
Torvald withholds stories he heard about Studlock
Studlock strongly feels that four guards are sufficient and no more should be hired
Torvald goes to his tiny office in the barracks annex,
Torvald feels worried Lady Verada is ignorant of the compound guards’ past and reputation as mass murderers, sadists, and possibly not human
Torvald sneaks out the back window of the annex into the roof
Watches Lazan Door casting knuckle dice
Overhears telling Studlock that their options are running out fast and getting worse
Madrun said they had a choice to go north or south. They went south [Darujhistan] and regrets not going north
Madrun and Lazan Door threw away their masks, don’t want them. Studlock insists they make new ones
Torvald leaps the gap from the annex roof to the balcony of the main building and is immediately invited in for wine by Lady Verada
Lady Verada sits in a plush chair, hidden in the darkness. She wears a grey glove on her long fingered hand
Torvald says the castellan and compound guards are and vouches for Scorch and Leff, they’ll adjust to the job’s formality
Lady Verada wants Torvald to reconcile with his family in House Nom and praises his concern and loyalty, a trait of House Nom
Verada assures there won’t be negative consequences for seeking her out
Torvald leaves and summons Studlock to Lady Verada and reminds Madrun and Lazan of their guard duty
Both smile strangely, collect their scrying dice and resume their duty
Torvald returns to his tiny office
Leff thinks Tiserra is cursing Torvald as a witch because she hates that he’s working with them again
Narrator Kruppe tires of their bickering and directs the audience’s attention elsewhere
Kruppe walks down Great Avenue passing all the hard working people of Darujhistan
Produces wine and pastries from gods sleeve, spreading butter with a knife that has the Varada monogram on it
Kruppe enters Baruk’s estate, passing through all the magical wards to Baruk’s surprise
An obese toad demon snuggled by Kruppe’s feet as he sits down
Baruk finalized certain arrangements
Kruppe presents a consideration
A man who beats a man to death
A wealthy man that conspires to gouge the price of wheat, causing families to starve, die young, and enter the life of crime.
Asks are both acts of violence?
The rich prey on the poor, the structure of society collapses
Barathol and Chaur spent all day cleaning out an old bakery they plan to convert into a smithy

Copper drums in the back, purchased a portable plains Rhivi anvil whose owner died before it was delivered, a hammer made of Aren steel likely stolen from a Malazan smithy, and plans to purchase materials the next day
A woman leads a gang of thugs into the smithy
Barathol interrupts her to say the valves are open, any spark will burn a great part of the district
When threatening to hurt them, Barathol pulls out a Malazan cusser. The thugs leave
Mallet had given him an empty cusser. Unknown why in a crate of 12 munitions, the Moranth will add an empty shell
Barathol plans to buy some armor for Chaur
10 PM, Gaz leaves planning to kill somebody while his wife Thordy polished the slate stones in her garden
Scillara walks with her arm hooked with Duiker’s arm through the streets
Challice and Crokus walk through the High Markets of the Estate District, not knowing how close they are
On a rooftop, Rallick absorbs all the information Krute of Talient tells him

After school, Stonny tells Murillio her story. His ability to pay complete attention to her and listen makes her feel comfortable enough to open up her emotions and cry, easier every time. Murillio would stroke her hair and push away her tears
Three dozen assassins ready themselves to attack the ex-Bridgeburners
(Picker)
Picker looks down on the bar from her room on the second story
Twenty patrons, Fisher plays a sad melody, a stranger from Pale went to bed early in the corner room upstairs
Blend is ignored by patrons as usual, due to her talent [magic]
Antsy goes to calm down the two line cooks that hate each other and things wrong escalate, Picker usually has to go downstairs to fix it
Bluepearl explores more of the temple
(Bluepearl)
Bluepearl’s in the cellar looking through four casks hidden in a crawl space behind a shelf
Two were vinegar, one was cedar/pine sap
The fourth cask seemed like ancient magic, sealed with wax marked by the temple sigil, smelled like yeast, possibly had blood
A ghost appears from the floor and asks for Brother Cuven
Bluepearl takes the cask upstairs
(Stranger)
The stranger from Pale dug out the bars from the window to let assassins climb in
(Blend)
Blend watches five half drunk men, clothes suggesting they’re nobles, argue about the price of bread
(Antsy)
Antsy wields his shortsword looking for a two-headed rat in the storeroom, the cooks can attest seeing it
Plans to pickle it in a jar as a curio for the bar
(Assassins)
Eleven assassins enter the stranger from Pale’s room. Three had daggers, four had crossbows, four were big men that had swords, bucklers, and chain shirts
(Fisher)
The bard Fisher goes to get a drink off the side of the stage, as the nobles pick a table to sit down
(Picker)
Mallet walks into Picker’s room worried that the blacksmith guild might do something to Barathol and Chaur
Picker thinks the nobles are trouble, but then also hears something else. Mallet hears it too
Picker sees Blend pull her legs back from the table aware something bad is about to happen
(Blend)
Blend stands up and draws something from her raincape as the front door of the bar opens
(Antsy)
The rat runs into the cellar, Antsy chases it as Bluepearl walks out with the yeasty elder magic cask
Three cloaked figures enter
The first arrow fires into the bartender Skevos’ sternum
The second arrow fires towards Picker upstairs
The third arrow strikes Hedry, the 15 year old serving girl knocking her around
The five nobleman took out knives and attacked everyone around them
Blend lunges towards the crossbowmen
Slices the first target’s throat
Cuts the tendons of the second target’s arm
Dodges the first target falling down, stabs the third target’s chest through his chain and uppercut slices between his legs
Turns and slices the face of the second target. He tries to dodge back but hit his head hard on the low rafters and falls to his knees. Blend stabs him in the eye
A fourth crossbowman behind them fires into Blend’s shoulder. Blend is knocked around and loses sensation in her arm. The fourth lunges to her
(Mallet)
The downstairs quarrel that fired up stairs strikes the wall close to Mallet’s head
Mallet dodges into the hallway, the eleven assassins upstairs fire at him
A quarrel hits his stomach and rips through his throat
Mallet lands on his back, chokes on his blood, attempts to use High Denul
A young assassin stabs into his eye
Kick open the gate, Whiskeyjack
Mallet dies ☠
(Assassin)
The assassin that killed Mallet wonders why Mallet was smiling
(Bluepearl)
Bluepearl comes out of the kitchen into the taproom, a knife pins his hand to the cask
An assassin rushes with a knife, one behind comes with a long thin blade
Bluepearl spits at the knife-wielder, the globule transforming mid-air into a ball of a dozen serpents that bite at the assassin’s face. The assassin panics and stabs at his own face
Bluepearl tries to drop the cask, his hand falling with the cask pulling him down
The second assassin pierces Bluepearl through his nose into his brain. Bluepearl dies ☠
(Antsy)
At the cellar door, Antsy hears the sounds of the battle
The cook and two scullions run to the backdoor
Antsy runs into the store room, pulls open a crate and retrieves five moranth munitions
The cook and scullions run back inside as assassins try to enter through the alley
Antsy throws a sharper past them, detonating onto the wall behind the two assassins killing them
Antsy steps on top of the dead assassins and throws another sharper into the alley, killing a dozen assassins outside
(Picker)
Picker watches Mallet die and shuts the door
Rushes to her desk, opens the chest with her crossbow and sharper
Picker looks out and watches Blend get hit in the shoulder by the fourth marksman, Picker headshots that marksman. Blood, brain, and skull sprays behind him

The assassins in the hallway bust through the door, Picker throws the sharper at them and jumps out the window. Her office explodes as she lands on a table with two of her dead regulars. Her knee slams into her chin, cracking her teeth. Her quarrels scatter on the floor
Picker spits blood and gets back up
(Blend)
Blend watches the crossbowman get headshotted by Picker’s quarrel
Blend pulls the quarrel lodged in the cartilage between her upper arm and shoulder socket, Blend passes out
(Antsy)
Antsy pushes the cook and scullions into the alleyway and runs back inside, picking up a black cauldron lid as a shield
Antsy and Picker coordinates an attack on the assassins as they walk down the stairs
Antsy approaches to throw the sharper upstairs and bait two crossbow quarrels against the cauldron lid
An assassin leaps down towards Antsy, Picker fires at the assassin stomach killing her
Antsy rushes upstairs, Picker pulls him back and runs ahead of Antsy and kills the three assassins stunned and dying on the floor
Blend wakes up, arm still in pain, and sees six cloaked figures approaching to the front door
Blend picks up a dagger ready to fight
Chaur barrels into them crying, hands like mauls, snapping their necks and crushing their faces
Barathol follows up with his knife, making sure Chaur doesn’t die
Some of the assassins get up, Blend tries to rush forward but is pulled back by Antsy
Antsy attacks with his shortsword and cauldron lid
